07 Market Access And Procurement

Market access — how MFC would actually reach schools and workplaces

This file exists because one of the two URLs Hunter supplied turned out not to be a competitor at all — it is a market-access gate. Understanding it changes the sequencing of MFC's plans.

What the NSW catalogue actually is

verified fact The NSW Student Wellbeing external programs catalogue is "an online register of externally produced programs, quality assured by the department, and available to schools either free of charge or to purchase." Launched 2022 with ~50 programs; now ~60 quality-assured programs across ~57 providers.

Four themes: Respectful relationships and consent education · Positive student behaviour · Resilience building · Students' sense of belonging.

Criteria verified fact: programs must be evidence-based, relevant and inclusive, and aligned to the current curriculum and key departmental documents.

verified fact The quality assurance criteria were informed by a commissioned Literature Review undertaken by the Murdoch Children's Research Institute.

unknown The MCRI review itself was not located. It effectively encodes the evidence bar for the largest school system in Australia. Obtaining it is the single highest-value follow-up action in this entire research — it tells MFC exactly what standard its pilot must meet.

Entry route verified fact: periodic tender via NSW eTendering. There are no current tenders open as at 1 August 2026. Future tenders are announced on the Department of Education webpage.

Important: verified fact schools retain autonomy to choose non-catalogue programs. So the catalogue is a credibility accelerator and sales-cycle compressor, not a gate.

⭐ The actual gate — the principal's decision checklist

verified fact — extracted in full from "Choosing external student wellbeing programs — a guide for schools" (NSW DoE, 2024). This is the document a NSW principal completes and signs. It is the most operationally useful artefact in this entire research: it is a specification MFC can build against directly.

Section 2 — Mandatory criteria (five items)

"If the school is not provided with evidence of the above five (5) mandatory criteria, it is strongly recommended that the program is not implemented."

# Requirement
1 Public liability insurance — level required $20M
2 Workers compensation — if a sole trader, personal accident and injury insurance
3 Delivered by staff holding a current Working With Children Check (plus a check against the department's Not to Be Employed list)
4 Delivered by staff holding qualifications relevant to the program
5 If online and it collects or stores identifiable data, the school must clear it with the Information Technology Directorate (cyber.security@det.nsw.edu.au)

strategic hypothesis These five are pass/fail and have nothing to do with evidence. They are the cheapest possible barrier for MFC to clear and should be closed out before any school conversation. Note items 3 and 4 bear directly on D-0016's unresolved safeguarding items — the same work unblocks both. Note also that item 5 is a real constraint on any future MFC digital tool.

Section 3 — Evaluation criteria (the judgement layer)

Criterion What the principal must be satisfied of
Student need The program meets an identified student wellbeing need
Alignment & consultation Supports the School Excellence Plan · adds value to the curriculum · reviewed against departmental policies (e.g. Controversial Issues in Schools) · inclusive and safe for all students · caters for individual needs
Evidence base "The program has clear outcomes." · "There is evidence that the program has a positive impact on student wellbeing outcomes."
Functionality Feasible within school organisation (timetabling, space, time out of class, supervision, staff) · "There is a logical and consistent sequence to activities" · can be modified to context while maintaining core activities · "External providers have mechanisms to ensure the program is delivered with quality every time (fidelity)"
Feedback and ongoing improvement "The program builds capacity in staff members' skills and knowledge" · "There is a clear and rigorous process for evaluating the outcomes of this program in your school" (student, staff and parent feedback)

The principal then records: Purchase approved / Purchase declined / More information required, signed and dated, attached to the school's risk management proforma.

Why this matters more than the catalogue

inference Four observations, each with a direct implication:

  1. The evidence bar in the checklist is lower than expected. It asks for "clear outcomes" and "evidence that the program has a positive impact" — not RCTs, not effect sizes, not peer review. A well-designed pilot with pre/post capability data and an honest write-up would clear this. The catalogue tender bar is higher; the school-by-school bar is not.
  2. Fidelity and sequence are explicitly asked for — "a logical and consistent sequence to activities" and "mechanisms to ensure the program is delivered with quality every time." This is the checklist rewarding exactly what [[60-projects/market-and-competitor-intelligence-v1/02-profiles-australia-direct|Gotcha4Life fails to publish]] (no dosage) and what MFC's practice architecture is supposed to be. Publishing dosage and a fidelity mechanism converts an internal design decision into a procurement advantage.
  3. "Builds capacity in staff members' skills and knowledge" is a scored criterion. strategic hypothesis This is the checklist independently rewarding the adults-first design principle that RULER, Penn's MRT and Geelong Grammar all converged on. A program that trains only students scores worse than one that also builds teacher capability.
  4. The department tells schools to prefer the catalogue but explicitly permits going outside it. So MFC does not need to wait for a tender window to enter NSW schools — it needs to be able to complete this checklist. That reorders the sequencing conclusion below.

Who is already listed

Providers include: Smiling Mind · The Resilience Project · batyr · Healthy Minds Enterprises · Act for Kids · Australian Red Cross · Body Safety Australia · Consent Labs · Grow Your Mind · Open Parachute · Our Futures Institute · PCYC NSW · Save the Children · Top Blokes Foundation · The Peer Support Foundation · Youth Insearch · Raise Foundation, and ~40 others.

MFC is not listed. Four of the organisations profiled in this research are.

What schools are already required to teach

This is the part that determines whether MFC has a legitimate offer or a duplicate one.

verified fact Australian Curriculum HPE (Version 9) — two strands, both compulsory every year, Foundation to Year 10. The relevant strand is Personal, Social and Community Health, with three sub-strands: Identities and change · Interacting with others · Making healthy and safe choices. Underpinned by a strengths-based approach and focused on health literacy.

verified fact General Capability: Personal and Social Capability (V9) — 4 elements, 14 sub-elements:

Element Sub-elements
Self-awareness personal awareness · emotional awareness · reflective practice
Self-management goal setting · emotional regulation · perseverance and adaptability
Social awareness empathy · relational awareness · community awareness
Social management communication · collaboration · leadership · decision-making · conflict resolution

verified fact Crucially: general capabilities are embedded within learning areas, not taught standalone — "best developed within the context of the learning area."

verified fact Australian Student Wellbeing Framework — five elements: leadership, inclusion, student voice, partnerships, support. A whole-school framework, not a curriculum.

verified fact Respectful Relationships (Victoria) — a core component of the Victorian Curriculum since 2016, F–12, in all government and Catholic schools; 1,950+ schools in the lead-and-partner initiative. Covers healthy relationships, problem-solving, consent, gender stereotypes, emotional literacy and resilience. Direct content overlap with any mental fitness offer in Victoria.

Duplicate vs genuine gap

inference What duplicates: emotion identification · help-seeking · self-regulation vocabulary · respectful-relationship content. All already mandated in HPE and Personal and Social Capability, and separately funded in Victoria. A provider arriving with "we teach students to name their emotions" is selling a school something it is already legally required to deliver.

strategic hypothesis The three genuine gaps — and all three are consistent with SWM-03:

  1. Practice and repetition. The curriculum specifies capability outcomes; it does not specify a practice regime. Schools teach the content once and cannot sustain it. "Mental reps" is a structural answer to a real, documented implementation problem — and it is MFC's most defensible non-duplicative claim.
  2. Educator and parent-side delivery — Be You covers professional learning about mental health, but the mental fitness practice framing is unoccupied.
  3. Transition points (primary→secondary, senior years) where wellbeing budgets concentrate and curriculum coverage thins.

strategic hypothesis Every school-facing MFC asset should map explicitly to HPE sub-strands and the 14 Personal and Social Capability sub-elements, and then show what the curriculum does not provide: sustained practice. That mapping is cheap to produce and does the procurement work.

Be You — the free incumbent

verified fact Australia's national mental health and wellbeing in education initiative, operating since 2018, delivered by Beyond Blue with Early Childhood Australia and headspace, funded by the Australian Government Department of Health, Disability and Ageing. Offers free evidence-based professional learning modules across five topic areas, plus tools, consultants, webinars and toolkits.

It is educator-facing professional learning, not a student program. Correct About URL: beyou.edu.au/about.

strategic hypothesis Do not build educator mental-health-literacy PD. Position alongside Be You — student- and practice-facing — and cite alignment with it. Complementarity is a procurement advantage; competing with a free, Commonwealth-funded national program is not.

Note also that Be You runs the programs directory that gave The Resilience Project its 4/4 evidence and 4/4 implementation rating — a third-party endorsement that shortens every school's procurement decision. That directory is a second market-access target alongside the NSW catalogue.

Where the money actually is

Source Detail Status
Student Wellbeing Boost $203.7m — $192m one-off to every school (~$20,000 average, need- and size-adjusted, for the 2023 school year) plus $10.8m for a mental health check tool verified fact One-off and now spent. Do not build a 2026 business case on it.
National Student Wellbeing Program Five-year $307.18m Federation Funding Agreement verified fact This is the recurrent money — but it primarily funds student wellbeing officers/chaplains, i.e. staffing, not program licences inference
NSW Student Wellbeing Innovation Fund $3.2m seed funding for innovative programs that could later enter the catalogue verified fact as announced 2022/23; current status unknown
School discretionary wellbeing budgets · P&C fundraising · state equity loadings Low thousands per school, decided by a principal or wellbeing leader inference

strategic hypothesis The money that reaches external program providers is largely school-level discretionary, in amounts of low thousands, decided one school at a time. That means the sale is ~1:1 and slow unless a catalogue listing or framework alignment does the trust work in advance. Catalogue entry is therefore less a revenue channel than a sales-cycle compressor — which is exactly why it matters.

Benchmark against this: The Resilience Project charges $3,900 + $20/student for a digital school partnership — roughly $15,900/year for a 600-student secondary school. The AIS Mental Fitness Program is free. inference MFC would be entering a market with a well-evidenced paid incumbent at ~$16k and a government-backed free alternative using MFC's own category name.

The sequencing conclusion

strategic hypothesis — for Hunter's decision.

Reading the market-access evidence alongside [[60-projects/market-and-competitor-intelligence-v1/01-category-language-and-positioning-risk|01]]:

  1. Every credible school channel is evidence-gated, and MFC has no outcome evidence. SWM-07 already records this. The pilot is not a product milestone — it is a market-access prerequisite. Nothing described in this file is purchasable without it.
  2. NSW catalogue entry is closed right now. That is a scheduling constraint, not a blocker. The actions it implies: set a standing watch on the tender page; obtain the MCRI literature review to reverse-engineer the evidence criteria; and time the pilot's evaluation to complete before the next tender window rather than after it.
  3. The schools market is the most crowded, most evidence-demanding and most price-compressed segment MFC could choose — and the adult segment, where MFC already operates, is the least contested. This is the second independent line of evidence pointing the same way.

Amendment — the checklist changes point 2

inference The principal's checklist (above) was obtained after the sequencing conclusion was first drafted, and it softens it. Revised:

  • Catalogue entry is not a precondition for entering NSW schools. The department explicitly permits schools to choose non-catalogue programs, and the school-level bar ("clear outcomes", "evidence of positive impact") is materially lower than the tender bar.
  • The binding constraint is therefore not the tender window — it is the five mandatory criteria plus a defensible pilot. Both are achievable without waiting.
  • Catalogue entry remains valuable as a sales-cycle compressor and credibility signal, but it is a phase-two objective, not a gate.

Adjacent finding — Mental Health in Primary Schools (MHiPS)

verified fact Developed and run by the Centre for Community Child Health at MCRI and the Faculty of Education at University of Melbourne, in partnership with the Victorian Department of Education. Funded by the Victorian Government plus a large philanthropic syndicate (Ian Potter Foundation, Tim Fairfax Family Foundation, Helen McPherson Smith Trust, Bupa, The Ross Trust, and others). Implemented in Victoria and Queensland.

The model: creates a new Mental Health and Wellbeing Leader role inside the school, supported by systemic evidence-based professional development and SEL curriculum integration. Does not use "mental fitness" language.

inference Two things matter here. First, MCRI is both the author of the NSW evidence criteria and the operator of a competing school-capability model — worth understanding before approaching them. Second, MHiPS is the school-capability answer (build an internal role) rather than the external-provider answer (buy a program). strategic hypothesis That is the same structural insight as Smiling Mind's teacher-delivered model and RULER's cascade: the durable play in schools is building internal capability, not delivering external content. Three independent Australian and international examples now point the same way.

Named gaps in this research

  • The MCRI commissioned literature review for the NSW catalogue — still not located unknown. Now lower priority, because the operational checklist has been obtained directly and reveals the applied bar. Still worth having for a tender submission.
  • Per-jurisdiction commencement dates for the psychosocial Code — approximate; confirm before any compliance-adjacent claim unknown
  • Enforcement volume under Australian psychosocial WHS provisions unknown
  • Market size for Australian workplace mental health training post-2022 unknown
  • Be You programs directory submission criteria and process unknown

08 Strategic World Model Contradictions

Strategic World Model contradictions

A-17's role card requires: "Flag any finding that contradicts a Strategic World Model organisational position." This file discharges that obligation.

A-17 has no authority to change any SWM entry. Per the role card: advisory, no approval, no publication, no merge; corrections propagate to the SWM via A-05; and the human gate is "Hunter: any conclusion implying a change to MFC positioning." Every row below is a proposed change awaiting decision.

Contradicted entries

🔴 SWM-02 — Category — contradicted
Current statement "MFC is defining mental fitness as a category distinct from mental health treatment"
Classification mfc-organisational-position
Confidence high
Source Kernel K-05; D-0034

The contradiction. The term is already in definitional use by Gotcha4Life (since ~2017 — mission statement, tagline, program name, product name, founder's title) and Smiling Mind (since a formal September 2024 repositioning to "Lifelong Mental Fitness", with a named five-pillar framework). It is the literal name of the government-backed AIS Mental Fitness Program (with Black Dog Institute, ~2020, 90,000+ students, free, national). BetterUp published MFC's exact mental-health-vs-mental-fitness distinction in March 2021. MindUP has used "mental fitness tools" for twenty years. The US Army used it officially in 2009.

What is NOT contradicted. The distinction K-05 draws is real, sharper than any competitor's, and does genuine work. The boundary against clinical treatment (K-04) holds cleanly against Beyond Blue, headspace, Black Dog and ReachOut. The problem is the word "defining", not the content.

Proposed change — for Hunter: - Classification: mfc-organisational-position → retain, but - Confidence: high → low, and - Statement: consider revising from defining the category to something the evidence supports. Candidate wording in [[60-projects/market-and-competitor-intelligence-v1/01-category-language-and-positioning-risk|01]]: "Australia has been told what mental fitness is. Nobody has yet shown what training it actually takes." - Add review_trigger: "any competitor category-language change; any certification-shaped MFC product naming decision."

🔴 SWM-14 — Sector condition — contradicted and materially understated
Current statement "Adjacent Australian organisations occupy nearby space (Smiling Mind, Gotcha4Life)"
Classification market-observation · Confidence low · Source: "Candidate list only — not researched"

The contradiction. Now researched. "Nearby space" understates it: both named organisations use MFC's category term definitionally, and the list is materially longer — AIS/Black Dog, Mental Fitness Australia (certification trade marks), Danny Frawley Centre, MensLine, Uprise, plus The Resilience Project and R U OK? competing for the same budgets without the term.

Proposed change: - Confidence: low → high - Source: → this objective - Statement: rewrite to reflect direct category-language competition, not adjacency - Split into multiple entries — the current single entry cannot carry what is now known

🟡 SWM-06 — Differentiation — partially contradicted
Current statement "Recognition before abstraction; non-moralising; practice over information"
Confidence medium

The tension. Practice over information is the right diagnosis — but the training-transfer literature says a workshop, by itself, does not produce sustained practice (Blume et al. 2010; Broad & Newstrom 1992 — skills decay to baseline within six months absent ongoing support). And no organisation anywhere — including RULER, Triple P and Penn — has published evidence that its program builds a durable lifelong practice.

So practice over information differentiates MFC's intent, not yet its delivery. It is currently a claim about what MFC values, not about what MFC produces.

Proposed change: retain the statement; add a review_trigger tied to the first pilot; and record explicitly that the differentiation is unevidenced by anyone in the field, not merely unevidenced by MFC.

🟡 SWM-13 — Risk / may-be-wrong — strengthened, and should be upgraded
Current statement "The category claim assumes the public experiences a knowing–doing gap in these terms. Untested externally."
Classification strategic-hypothesis · Confidence low

The finding. This entry is correct and more important than its confidence rating suggests. Two pieces of external evidence now bear on it:

  1. Smiling Mind tested the adjacent question and published it — 900 Australians, nearly half aged 5–18, finding people conflate "mental health" with "mental illness". They then repositioned the organisation on that finding and attracted $3.3M in federal funding. The move MFC has not made, a competitor made — with evidence.
  2. The MYRIAD trial returned a well-powered independent null for universal school-based mindfulness — meaning the broader universal-preventive-practice thesis is live and contested, not established.

Proposed change: retain classification; raise priority. Recommend adding a review_trigger: "resolved by an MFC-commissioned public comprehension study." This is identified across three files as the single highest-value piece of research MFC could commission.

🟢 SWM-07 — Evidence gap — confirmed, and its strategic meaning inverted

Current: "No MFC-specific outcome evidence exists — no pilot has run." verified-fact, high confidence. Unchanged and correct.

But its meaning changes. Currently framed as a deficit. The research suggests it is also MFC's largest single opportunity:

  • Every strong evidence base in this field is developer-conducted — RULER (disclosed COI plan), Triple P (32 of 33 studies developer-affiliated, no registered trials, two COI statements), US Army MRT (developer paid for delivery). The one program with genuine independent multi-country replication — KiVa — is the one that scaled internationally.
  • Nobody has published a dose-response curve for adult non-clinical mental fitness training. The Resilience Project's evidence shows nothing measurable before year 6.
  • Nobody has a performance-based measure of capability. RULER's own authors concede the field lacks assessments "sensitive to change."

strategic hypothesis MFC having no evidence yet means MFC is the only player free to design its first study around the question the whole sector is avoiding — and to do it with pre-registration, pre-specified outcomes, a published COI statement and an arm's-length evaluator holding the right to publish nulls. These cost almost nothing at pilot stage and are effectively unpurchasable retrospectively.

Proposed addition: a new SWM entry capturing evidence-design-as-strategic-asset.

Proposed new entries

The SWM records seven dimensions with no seeded entry, described as "the honest gaps." This research populates several. Proposed additions, for A-05 to action if Hunter approves:

Proposed Dimension Statement Class Conf
SWM-17 Threats Training sits at the bottom of the WHS hierarchy of controls; a mental fitness program cannot discharge an employer's psychosocial duty. Fleming (2024, n=46,336) found participants in individual-level interventions no better off than non-participants, with small effects and credible intervals mostly crossing zero; cross-sectional, and the author's own reading is selection bias rather than harm verified-fact high
SWM-18 Partnership landscape Black Dog Institute is both the clinical partner of the competing AIS Mental Fitness Program and a potential MFC partner — it supplies credibility to a program that has not defined the concept or built a practice layer strategic-hypothesis medium
SWM-19 Funding model Three proven non-profit revenue architectures exist: free-core + paid organisational (Humin); trademark licensing on 3–5 yr fee-plus-royalty (KiVa); institutional package + annual subscription (RULER). Practitioner accreditation (Triple P, MHFA) is simultaneously scaling mechanism, quality control and revenue market-observation high
SWM-20 Threats MFC has no stated position on Indigenous Social and Emotional Wellbeing (SEWB) — an established, Indigenous-led, policy-recognised Australian wellbeing framework. A claim to define a wellbeing category in Australia engages it directly unresolved-question high
SWM-21 Audience segments The general adult population seeking sustained non-clinical skill development outside a school or annual campaign is the least contested segment. The schools market is the most crowded, evidence-demanding and price-compressed strategic-hypothesis medium
SWM-22 Public and social need No MFC-commissioned public comprehension evidence exists. Smiling Mind commissioned the adjacent study (n=900), published it, repositioned on it, and attracted $3.3M federal funding verified-fact high
SWM-23 Cultural/behavioural trends The dominant global association of "mental fitness" is now enterprise employee performance (BetterUp, ~$5B). Absent active public definition by MFC, that becomes the default public meaning — the opposite of K-00 strategic-hypothesis medium

What A-17 is NOT concluding

Per the role card's exclusions and stop conditions:

  • No recommendation on what MFC should do about any of this. That is A-18/A-25's question and Hunter's decision.
  • No legal conclusion on the trade mark position. The composite-mark analysis in [[60-projects/market-and-competitor-intelligence-v1/01-category-language-and-positioning-risk|01]] is a reading of public material, not advice. An IP Australia register search and qualified advice are required before any certification-shaped product is named.
  • No position on SEWB. Recorded as an unowned risk requiring Indigenous-led resolution. Recommend routing to A-12.
  • No criticism of any competitor unsupported by evidence. Every negative finding is sourced or explicitly labelled inference.
  • No inference of any competitor's internal strategy, finances or effectiveness from marketing material.

Escalation

Routed to A-05 for SWM entry lineage. Escalated to Hunter under the A-17 human gate: any conclusion implying a change to MFC positioning. SWM-02 is a load-bearing organisational position and this research contradicts it.

09 Five Page Findings

Where MFC actually stands

A five-page read of 30+ organisations, five adjacent fields, and MFC's own workshop package. Everything here is sourced. Nothing is a decision — A-17 characterises; Hunter decides.

Page 1 — The situation

The finding, in one line

The word is taken. The category is vacant.

At least fourteen organisations use "mental fitness" — two Australian charities definitionally, a free government-backed schools program as its literal name, and a 234,000-person annual event as its strapline. But six of the highest-profile users, including Black Dog Institute, never define it at all. Six mutually incompatible definitions are in use among those who do. There is no validated measure of the construct anywhere in the world.

And underneath all of it sits an Australian, peer-reviewed, expert-consensus definition from 2015 that nobody cites — which MFC has independently converged on.

What contradicts the current position

SWM-02 records, at high confidence, that MFC is defining mental fitness as a category. The evidence does not support that as stated — but it supports something better. See page 5.

Claimant Usage Since
Gotcha4Life Mission, tagline, "Mentally Fit Schools", "Mental Fitness Gym", founder titled "Mental Fitness Advocate" ~2017
Smiling Mind Formally repositioned to "Lifelong Mental Fitness" with a named five-pillar framework Sept 2024
AIS Mental Fitness Program (AIS + Black Dog Institute) The literal program name. Free, national, 90,000+ students, 458 schools ~2020
BetterUp Published MFC's exact mental-health-vs-mental-fitness distinction March 2021
US Army "Comprehensive Soldier Fitness addresses mental fitness" — US$125m 2009
Mental Fitness Australia · MindUP · Positive Intelligence · Danny Frawley Centre · Uprise · MensLine Various — one holds ACCC-assessed certification trade marks —

The uncomfortable one: Smiling Mind reached MFC's founding insight independently — surveying 900 Australians, finding people conflate "mental health" with "mental illness" — published it, and repositioned the whole organisation on it (Sept 2024). That is MFC's argument, evidenced, by a competitor.

Correction, 2026-08-05 — the $3.3M causal link in this sentence was wrong, verified against the primary source. The Federal Government's $3.3M announcement (blog.smilingmind.com.au/federal-funding-announcement-smiling-mind-0eree) is dated 29 April 2022 — over two years before the Sept 2024 stigma-research/repositioning. The government's own stated rationale was the Schools Program's existing reach (200,000+ children, 1,200 schools) and prevention framing, not the 900-person comprehension study. 02-profiles-australia-direct.md line 180 already had this scoped correctly ("to roll the Schools Program out"); this file's causal chain — research → repositioning → funding — does not hold up chronologically and should not be repeated. The research and the funding are both real Smiling Mind facts; they are not causally connected the way this sentence implied.

What is not contradicted

K-05 — "Mental health is how we are doing. Mental fitness is what we are able to do" — is the sharpest articulation any organisation in this landscape has produced. No competitor has an equivalent one-liner. The boundary against clinical treatment holds cleanly against Beyond Blue, headspace, Black Dog and ReachOut.

The problem is the word "defining", not the content. MFC is not creating a category. It is entering one that two established charities are actively building — and it has a better definition than either.

Page 2 — The landscape, and the hole in it

Everyone claimed the gym. Nobody built it.

Organisation What they promise What the numbers show
Gotcha4Life A "Mental Fitness Gym" 114,177 workshop participants → 9,566 gym members = 8%
Smiling Mind "Lifelong" Mental Fitness 9.8M downloads · no retention data published
AIS Mental Fitness "strategies to stay mentally fit" 85% "likely to implement" — an intention measure
R U OK? A conversation skill Peak-day awareness · no skill measurement at all
The Resilience Project Whole-school wellbeing The field's best evidence — showing nothing measurable before year 6

That last row is the single most important number in this research. Balasooriya Lekamge et al. (2025), BJPsych Open, n=40,149 across 102 schools: no significant difference at 2–3 years. Effects appear only at 6+ years. Most schools don't stay six years.

The four evidence positions

Best evidence What it actually shows
Gotcha4Life None published in 8 years Post-only self-report %s, undisclosed n
Smiling Mind Pilot feasibility CRCT, n=188 preschoolers Feasibility — not efficacy
The Resilience Project Quasi-experimental, n=40,149, peer-reviewed Real — and dose-dependent to 6 years
R U OK? Cross-sectional survey, n=2,013 Association, not causation

What everyone shares as a weakness

Every strong evidence base in this field is developer-conducted. RULER (disclosed COI plan). Triple P — a BMC Medicine review found 32 of 33 studies developer-affiliated, zero registered trials, two COI statements, and independent Dutch trials found no advantage over care-as-usual. The US Army's MRT (developer paid to deliver).

The one program with genuine independent multi-country replication — KiVa — is the one that scaled internationally. That is not a coincidence.

The structural forces nobody flagged

  1. Training sits at the bottom of the WHS hierarchy of controls. A mental fitness program cannot discharge an employer's psychosocial duty — the Code requires work redesign first. And Fleming (2024), n=46,336 across 233 organisations, found no wellbeing benefit from individual-level interventions, with resilience-training participants reporting worse mental health. (Cross-sectional, so likely selection — but the headline has landed with buyers.)
  2. Schools already must teach this. HPE's Personal, Social and Community Health strand is compulsory F–10; Personal and Social Capability specifies 14 sub-elements including emotional regulation. "We teach students to name emotions" sells schools something they're legally required to deliver already.
  3. Be You is free, Commonwealth-funded, and owns educator-facing PD.
  4. Indigenous SEWB — an Indigenous-led, policy-recognised Australian wellbeing framework with seven domains — exists, and MFC has no stated position on it.

Page 3 — What is actually MFC's

Testing MFC's three signature elements against the prior art produced the most useful — and least comfortable — findings in the research. Two are rediscoveries. One appears genuinely unclaimed.

Element Verdict
Stop, Shift, Do Not novel. Six named protocols occupy the identical three-slot structure; two share the first word
The Radar Not novel — it is implementation intentions (Gollwitzer, 1993/99). But a real under-researched variant sits inside it
The access gap Not novel as theory — restates Tulving & Pearlstone (1966). Possibly novel as a public-programme organising principle
The outcome-independent rep ⭐ Genuinely unclaimed. No program found that counts practice by attempt rather than result

Stop-Shift-Do is a crowded genre

Protocol Origin ① Interrupt ② Shift ③ Act
Stop, Shift, Do MFC Stop Shift Do
DBT STOP Linehan, 1993 Stop Step back · Observe Proceed mindfully
MBSR STOP Goldstein, 2012 Stop Take a breath · Observe Proceed
SBNRR Google / Search Inside Yourself, 2012 Stop Breathe · Notice · Reflect Respond
Meta-Moment Brackett / Yale Sense the shift Pause · See best self Strategise & Act
Choice Point Harris (ACT), ~2015 Notice the hook Name the choice point Towards move
PQ rep Chamine, 2012 Intercept Saboteur 10-sec PQ rep Sage response

Two independent traditions — DBT and MBSR — converged on an identical four-step "STOP." That convergence is evidence the structure is a natural solution, not an invention.

hypothesis Claiming Stop-Shift-Do as a model is a credibility liability any clinician will spot in thirty seconds. Treat it as a wording choice within an established genre and cite the lineage — Linehan, Goldstein, Tan, Brackett, Harris.

⚠ The Radar is implementation intentions

Pre-selecting everyday situations in advance in order to notice and act when they arise is Gollwitzer's implementation intentions — and the mechanism he describes (pre-specifying a cue heightens its perceptual accessibility and automates cue→response retrieval) is precisely what the Radar claims to do. 94 tests, d = .65; 642 tests by 2024.

The genuine difference is narrow but real: implementation intentions pre-specify cue and response; the Radar pre-specifies cue only, leaving the response to in-moment judgement.

hypothesis That cue-open variant is genuinely under-researched — Gollwitzer's evidence is for fully specified plans. If MFC wants a research claim, that is it. But the Radar must stop being described as an original insight; not citing Gollwitzer looks either uninformed or evasive.

Note this makes "add implementation intentions to the workshop close" not an addition but a decision: close the response slot (proven, d=.65) or leave it open (novel, untested). Choose knowingly.

The access gap restates a 60-year-old finding

Tulving & Pearlstone (1966) drew the availability vs accessibility distinction in those exact words. Whitehead (1929) named inert knowledge. Arnsten (2009) supplies the neuroscience of skills you have but cannot reach. Sheppes et al. (2011) on emotion-regulation choice and Bonanno & Burton (2013) on regulatory flexibility are the closest academic analogues — K-04's "access and coordinate relevant human skills across changing situations" is close to a paraphrase of them.

But no lay-facing public-health programme was found whose headline claim is "you already have the skills; the gap is access." inference Not new knowledge — a new packaging position. Cited, it reads as sophisticated translation work. Uncited, it reads as naive.

⭐ The outcome-independent rep — plant the flag here

"The outcome does not determine whether it counts."

Close cousins exist (ACT's towards-moves, Bjork's learning-vs-performance, Dweck's process praise) — but no program operationalises a countable practice unit defined by attempt rather than result. Fitness reps are counted exactly this way, which is why the metaphor works.

It is teachable, falsifiable, and it makes a research programme possible — rep count becomes an exposure variable. This and the measurement gap on page 4 are the same asset viewed from two sides.

Three problems to fix

1. A seam three separate critiques converge on. K-04 lists power, safety, environment, support among the determinants of access — a structural claim. But the intervention is purely individual: reps at pre-chosen moments. The individualisation critique, the WHS hierarchy of controls, and the prior-art audit all find the same unresolved tension. Either the model addresses environmental access, or the framing narrows.

2. The differentiating framework isn't published. verified The public site carries no Radar, no Stop-Shift-Do, no access framing. It runs a "Daily 1% Model" — 14 minutes a day of breathwork, mindfulness, gratitude, connection, visualisation — which sits very close to Smiling Mind, the Push-Up Challenge and Positive Intelligence. The distinctive part is in the vault; the published part is the least distinctive part.

3. 🛑 The public site contradicts the locked kernel. verified It frames mental fitness as "mental muscles" — "think about it like mental muscles, with Mental Reps used to build mental muscles."

K-04, verbatim: "The comparison is explanatory, not literal: the mind is not a muscle."

The public site asserts as its central explanatory device the precise analogy the locked kernel prohibits taking literally. It also carries a third definition, matching neither K-04 nor the internal one. Live instance of C-13, on the public record.

And note: Positive Intelligence has owned "mental fitness + reps + brain muscles" since 2012. That is the exact territory the public site occupies.

Where the design is thin — honestly

Issue Evidence
Dosage is a single session + one self-set reminder + one retrieval prompt at 3–4 weeks Broad & Newstrom: skills decay to baseline within six months without ongoing support. Blume et al. (2010) meta-analysis: only a modest portion of training transfers
Follow-up ends at 3–4 weeks Lally et al. (2010): median 66 days to automaticity (range 18–254). The measurement window closes before habit formation would be expected
WHO-5 is the primary instrument WHO-5 measures "how we are doing" — the mental health side of K-05. MFC's own headline measure is of the thing its category definition says it is not about
No implementation-intention structure at close Gollwitzer & Sheeran (2006), 94 tests, 8,000+ participants: d = .65 on goal attainment. Free to add

To MFC's credit, the package is honest about all of this — it explicitly claims no validated cadence, and requires WHO-5 change to be reported descriptively with no causal claim. That discipline is rarer than it should be.

What MFC already does that the sector doesn't

Two items in the Stage 10 measurement design are genuinely ahead of the field:

  • The initial-use item — "did you attempt a mental rep in any of the three moments — even once?" This is a behavioural attempt measure. Gotcha4Life, Smiling Mind and AIS all publish satisfaction or intention instead.
  • The opportunity-sensitivity item — "Did any of those moments come up at all, whether or not you tried a rep?" This distinguishes no opportunity from opportunity, no attempt. That is a COM-B Opportunity check, and essentially nobody in this market does it.

Page 4 — What we can actually use

The question was "is there anything beneficial?" Yes — eleven things, ranked by cost-to-value.

Free, do now

1. The NSW principal's checklist is a build-against specification. Obtained in full. Five mandatory pass/fail criteria — $20M public liability insurance · workers compensation · WWCC · relevant qualifications · cyber clearance if storing identifiable data. Then judgement criteria that explicitly reward "a logical and consistent sequence to activities", "mechanisms to ensure the program is delivered with quality every time (fidelity)", and "builds capacity in staff members' skills and knowledge."

Two consequences: the evidence bar at school level is "clear outcomes" and "evidence of positive impact" — not RCTs. And schools may choose non-catalogue programs, so MFC does not need to wait for a tender window. Items 3–4 overlap D-0016's safeguarding work — the same effort unblocks both.

2. Add implementation intentions to the close of every workshop. d = .65, 94 tests. MFC already captures "one possible next move" per moment — converting that to an explicit if-then ("when X happens, I will Y") is a wording change with a meta-analytic evidence base behind it.

3. Publish dosage. Nobody in the Australian set publishes session length, count and frequency clearly — Gotcha4Life publishes none at all. The NSW checklist explicitly rewards sequence and fidelity. Radical dosage transparency is free and immediately differentiating.

4. Use "missing one day doesn't matter" as a public message. Lally et al. found skipping one opportunity did not materially affect habit formation. It is true, evidence-backed, permission-giving — and nobody is saying it. It also aligns exactly with MFC's outcome-independent rep.

5. Name and publish "Stop, Shift, Do" as the front door. It is MFC's ALEC. It exists. It is not being used.

Cheap, decide soon

6. Design the first pilot for evidence credibility, not just outcomes. Pre-register · pre-specify primary outcomes · publish a COI statement · use at least one non-self-report measure · retain an arm's-length evaluator with the contractual right to publish nulls. Near-zero cost now; unpurchasable retrospectively. This is the single lesson from Triple P, RULER and CSF combined.

7. Make repetition frequency the primary outcome. Not satisfaction, not wellbeing, not intention. Nobody has published a dose-response curve for adult non-clinical mental fitness training. MFC's existing initial-use and opportunity items are already 80% of the way there — they need a frequency count and a longer window.

8. Extend the follow-up past 66 days. The current 3–4 week window closes before the evidence says change would appear.

9. Replace WHO-5 as the headline instrument — and there is a specific, free, Australian answer.

The field's standard battery — WHO-5, K10, SWEMWBS, PERMA, SDQ — all measures state. That is why a program like MFC's cannot evidence its distinctive claim with it: the standard battery is instrumented for the category MFC says it is not in.

A concrete alternative exists, and it is cheap:

Layer Instrument Cost
Capability (knowing) STEM-B — 18-item situational judgement test of emotion management, α=.68; author Carolyn MacCann is at the University of Sydney Free
Self-perceived capability CompACT-15 — psychological flexibility: Openness · Behavioural Awareness · Valued Action; demonstrated measurement invariance over time Free
Behaviour (doing) Event-contingent EMA via SEMA3 — built at the University of Melbourne Free
Contrast/safety K10, or SWEMWBS as a secondary so funders get the number they recognise Free / £75

Avoid AAQ-II — Wolgast (2014) and Tyndall et al. (2019) showed it measures distress, not flexibility. A state measure masquerading as a process measure is precisely the error MFC's positioning exists to name.

Strategic, for decision

10. Make the measurement protocol itself the fundable proposition.

hypothesis This is the strongest single move available to MFC, and it turns the evidence gap from a liability into an asset.

Nobody measures how often, in real life, a person actually deployed a capability when an opportunity arose. Everything measures knowing, believing, or feeling. That is exactly MFC's construct — and MFC has already invented the metric on paper without naming it. The Stage 10 forms ask "did you attempt a rep?" (numerator) and "did any of those moments come up at all?" (denominator). Event-contingent EMA turns that single retrospective question into a repeated in-the-moment count:

Skill-use rate = reps deployed ÷ opportunities that arose. Plus rep frequency, latency to first unprompted rep, and maintenance at 4/8/12 weeks.

The pitch to funders and academic partners is not "we ran a program and people liked it." It is:

The field concedes it has no performance-based, change-sensitive measure of emotional capability. We are building the first evaluation that measures skill enactment in real life, using free Australian-built infrastructure. Whether the program works or not, the measurement protocol is a contribution.**

That is fundable for a charity with zero evidence, and defensible to a methodologist. It also creates natural partnership hooks — Melbourne for SEMA3, Sydney for STEM/STEU — which supply the ethics pathway and the statistical capability MFC lacks internally.

Caveats to design around: EMA compliance attrition is the standard failure mode (pre-register the threshold), and prompting about reps may itself increase reps (needs EMA in both arms or a delayed-EMA control).

11. Commission the public comprehension study. Does the Australian public distinguish how we are doing from what we are able to do? SWM-13 flags this as untested. Smiling Mind ran the adjacent study and published it. It would make the category claim evidenced rather than asserted.

Correction, 2026-08-05: the "converted it into $3.3M" clause repeated the same false causal link corrected above (47) — the $3.3M predates the study by two years and funded a different program for a different stated reason. The comprehension study's value case stands on its own (a citable stat, informing wording, category evidence) — it doesn't need, and shouldn't lean on, an inaccurate funding-outcome story.

12. Treat Black Dog Institute as a potential partner, not only a competitor. They supply clinical credibility to the AIS Mental Fitness Program — a program that never defines "mental fitness" and has no practice layer. Those are the two things MFC has.

Design patterns worth stealing

From Pattern
RULER Adults first, justified by theory: you cannot teach regulation from an unregulated adult. Also: leave behind reusable objects, not remembered ideas
US Army MRT The 5:3 "live it / teach it" ratio; skills named as verbs and moves ("Hunt the Good Stuff"); a daily shared ritual that makes reps social and public
Geelong Grammar "Learn it, live it, teach it, embed it" — the same adults-first principle, independently derived
Triple P Tiered universal-to-targeted design. Nobody in Australian mental fitness has one. It solves the reach-vs-depth tension directly
MHFA / KiVa / Triple P Licensed facilitator accreditation as scaling mechanism, quality control and revenue simultaneously. MHFA has been self-funding on this since 2002
Iceland's Planet Youth Population change came from changing what people did with their time and with whom — not what they were taught. If reps happen in real life, the environment may matter more than the workshop
Sparklers (NZ) Get a government ministry to commission your external evaluation — cheapest credibility available, and it produces curriculum-alignment mapping

Page 5 — What needs deciding

The one strategic call

SWM-02 says MFC is defining the category. That is wrong as stated — but the correction is an upgrade, not a retreat.

The category is genuinely vacant. Six of the biggest users never define it. Six incompatible definitions among those who do. No validated measure anywhere. And an orphaned Australian expert-consensus definition — Robinson, Oades & Caputi (2015), International Journal of Wellbeing, 25-expert Delphi panel — that says:

"Mental fitness is the modifiable capacity to utilise resources and skills to flexibly adapt to challenges... enabling thriving."

Compare K-04's evidence definition:

"a developable capacity to access and coordinate relevant human skills across changing situations."

These are close to the same sentence. MFC independently arrived at the published expert-consensus definition of its own category.

That converts MFC's position from "we assert a definition" to "we adopt and complete the published expert-consensus definition" — at zero cost, with immediate academic standing, and an obvious Australian partnership hook.

The defensible claim is therefore not that MFC invented the category. It is:

Australia has been told what mental fitness is, by fourteen organisations who don't agree and mostly don't define it. Nobody has finished the job — and nobody has ever measured it.

Two facts worth holding: the term was proposed to the APA by McCarthy in 1964 — it has been available and unclaimed for sixty years. And the sharpest boundary statement in the whole literature sits unadopted in Robinson's expert commentary: "mental fitness should be focusing on the process while mental health should focus on the outcome."**

How CASEL did exactly this — the playbook

CASEL coined "social and emotional learning" and owns it globally. The mechanism is legible and repeatable:

CASEL MFC equivalent
A convening, not a publication — the term and the organisation were both born at a single 1994 gathering at the Fetzer Institute, to "create a coherent framework and common vocabulary" Convene Robinson, Oades, Black Dog, Smiling Mind, Gotcha4Life, AIS, Movember, Push-Up Challenge. Robinson's 2015 Delphi is the pre-read. Claiming the definition takes nothing from incumbents who declined to define it
Codify fast, practitioner-first — a 1997 educators' guide, not a journal article A free practitioner framework — with a collective dimension built in, which no existing definition has
The CASEL 5 — small, memorable, includes relational competencies A small, nameable, countable competency set
Give it away — ownership came from adoption, not licensing Free and universally citable. The opposite of the Positive Intelligence / MTQ48 commercial-instrument model, which buys revenue at the cost of category leadership
Be the evidence infrastructure Publish the validated measure the field has promised since 1964. Whoever publishes the measure owns the construct

The fool's-errand version is a nice framework on a website. The real version is: definition + validated measure + free framework + adoption by others.

The sequencing call

Three independent lines of evidence point the same way:

  1. Category-language crowding — schools are where Gotcha4Life, Smiling Mind, TRP and the free AIS program all concentrate
  2. Price compression — TRP charges ~$15,900/yr for a 600-student school; AIS is free
  3. Evidence gating — every credible school channel requires outcome evidence MFC doesn't have yet

Meanwhile the general adult population, seeking sustained non-clinical skill development outside a school or an annual campaign, is the least contested segment in the landscape — and it is where MFC already delivers.

strategic hypothesis Treat adults as the position, not as a stepping stone to schools.

Open risks requiring human judgement

Risk Status
Indigenous SEWB — no MFC position exists on an Indigenous-led, policy-recognised Australian wellbeing framework Unowned. Requires Indigenous-led resolution, not an AI-drafted paragraph. Route to A-12
Trade mark — Mental Fitness Australia holds ACCC-assessed certification marks on "Certified Mental Fitness Star" and "Certified Mental Fitness First Responder" Composite marks, not the bare term — descriptive use is very unlikely to be blocked. But a certification-shaped MFC product would collide. IP Australia search + qualified advice before naming one
The individualisation critique — that everyday-practice framing shifts blame for structural problems onto individuals Has no good published answer from anyone in the field. MFC's K-04 boundary and outcome-independent rep are a better answer than most — but it must be led with, not defended
Inheriting CSF's critics — MFC claims the same metaphor a $125m program was attacked for Mitigated by piloting before scaling, publishing effect sizes not p-values, and independent evaluation

The eight actions, in order

Fix what's broken (this week) 1. The public site contradicts the locked kernel — "mental muscles" vs K-04's "the mind is not a muscle", plus a third definition matching neither. Live C-13 instance, on the public record. 2. Publish the differentiating framework. Radar, Stop-Shift-Do and the access framing are not on the site; the Daily 1% Model that is there is the least distinctive thing MFC has.

Claim what's yours (this quarter) 3. Cite the lineage — Gollwitzer for the Radar; Linehan/Goldstein/Tan/Brackett/Harris for the loop; Tulving/Sheppes/Bonanno & Burton for the access gap; Robinson et al. (2015) for the definition. Citing raises credibility; omitting invites the charge of ignorance or evasion. 4. Plant the flag on the outcome-independent rep — the one element with no prior claimant. 5. Decide the Radar's response slot knowingly — closed (proven, d=.65) or open (novel, untested). 6. Resolve the structural/individual seam in K-04, or narrow the framing. Three separate critiques converge on it.

Build the asset (this year) 7. Reopen D-0017 — swap WHO-5 off the primary slot for STEM-B + CompACT-15 (both free); keep a state measure as deliberate contrast, not headline. 8. Approach University of Melbourne (SEMA3) and University of Sydney (MacCann, STEM/STEU) — they supply the ethics pathway and statistical capability MFC lacks. 9. Pre-register the pilot; arm's-length evaluator with the right to publish nulls. Make skill-use rate the primary outcome; extend follow-up past 66 days. 10. Convene the definitional round table. This is the CASEL move, and the window is open.

Housekeeping 11. Close the five mandatory NSW criteria — insurance, workers comp, WWCC, qualifications, cyber. Overlaps D-0016. 12. IP Australia search before any certification-shaped naming; take advice on the Positive Intelligence overlap ("mental fitness + reps + brain muscles", 2012). 13. Open an Indigenous-led process on SEWB.

Honest limits of this research

Public sources only; no competitor's internals inferred from marketing. Two research streams failed and were recovered by direct research. Six adjacent fields remain thinner than intended — health insurer prevention, TGA app regulation, Men's Sheds/community models, ADF programs, lived-experience workforce, VIA character strengths — and are recorded as known gaps, not low priority. Unverifiable claims are marked unknown rather than estimated: TRP revenue, Gotcha4Life dosage, R U OK? current reach, the MCRI literature review, WHS enforcement volume.

10 Measurement White Space

Measurement — the white space, and how to occupy it

This is the single most actionable finding in the entire research. The field concedes it cannot measure the thing MFC's category is named after. The instruments to do it partly exist, are free, and two of the three are Australian.

Labels: verified = confirmed on a fetched primary source · claim = vendor/publisher assertion · inference · hypothesis · unknown.

The problem, stated precisely

RULER's own authors (Nathanson et al., 2016) concede the field lacks "developmentally sequenced, performance-based assessments of the full range of EI skills" that are "sensitive to change."

Everything in the standard wellbeing-evaluation battery measures one of three things:

What it measures Instruments Is it K-05 mental fitness?
How you feel / how you're doing K10, WEMWBS/SWEMWBS, PERMA Profiler, SDQ, WHO-5 ❌ No — this is the mental health side
What you believe you can do DERS, CompACT, ERQ Partly — self-perceived capability
Whether you know what to do MSCEIT, STEM, STEU, SELweb Closer — procedural knowledge
Whether you actually did it, in life (essentially nothing) ✅ This is K-05. And it is empty.

inference The structural point: every instrument in the field's standard battery measures state. That is precisely why a program like MFC's cannot demonstrate its distinctive claim using the standard battery — the standard battery is instrumented for the category MFC says it is not in.

The immediate implication for MFC's own design

verified MFC's Stage 10 measurement architecture (D-0017) uses WHO-5 as its instrument at all three timepoints.

WHO-5 measures how a person is doing. It sits on the mental health side of K-05. MFC's headline instrument measures the thing its own category definition says it is not about.

To MFC's credit, the package already requires WHO-5 change to be "reported descriptively only... no causal wellbeing claim may be drawn." The discipline is right. But the instrument still can't evidence the claim MFC exists to make. inference

What exists — the honest audit

Performance-based ability measures

MSCEIT (Mayer–Salovey–Caruso, V2) — 141 items, 30–45 min, age 17+, four branches. verified - Total-score test–retest r = .86; total α ≈ .79 — but subscale alphas range .34–.77 (Fiori et al., PLOS ONE 2014; Maul 2012). verified - The scoring problem: correctness is defined by consensus — the modal response of a norm sample. Fiori et al.'s IRT analysis found high scores can reflect conformity to the majority rather than emotional insight. verified This is the field's central attack line. - Cost: MHS-published, Qualification Level B, distributed in Australia via PAA and ACER on a token system; ~US$55–65/report retail, research rate ~US$15/subject claim. Exact current AU research rate unknown. - inference Verdict: wrong instrument for a first pilot. Expensive, gated, weak subscale reliability, and no published evidence it is sensitive to short program-induced change.

STEM and STEU — MacCann & Roberts (2008), Emotion 8(4), 540–551. The most important finding in this section. verified - STEU — 42 items. Presents an emotional situation; respondent selects the most likely resulting emotion. The scoring key is derived from Roseman's appraisal theory — theoretically derived, not consensus. This is the critical psychometric distinction from MSCEIT. α = .71 - STEM — 44 items. A situational judgement test of emotion management: what is the most effective action here. Items built from qualitative interviews, scored by expert judgement. α = .68 - STEM-B — Allen et al. (2015), an 18-item brief form developed via IRT and latent class analysis. verified - Cost: free. Items and scoring keys are published as supplementary material to MacCann & Roberts (2008) and in APA PsycTESTS. verified - Carolyn MacCann is now at the University of Sydney. verified — a live Australian academic relationship. - inference Verdict: the closest existing off-the-shelf instruments to "what you are able to do." Australian-connected, free, defensible. α ≈ .68–.71 is adequate for group-level pre/post comparison in a pilot — not for individual feedback or high-stakes claims. - unknown Whether STEM/STEU have any published sensitivity-to-change evidence. If none exists, that is itself a finding — and a reason to pair them with EMA rather than rely on them alone.

The honest caveat on all SJTs inference: an SJT measures knowing what to do, not doing it. One step closer to capability than sentiment; one step short of behaviour. MFC should say this out loud rather than let a funder over-read it.

Self-report — and one instrument to avoid

Instrument Measures Cost Verdict
K10 / K6 Psychological distress, past 4 weeks Free, public domain verified Pure state. Useful as a deliberate contrast/safety measure
SWEMWBS Positive mental wellbeing, 7 items Licensed — £75 (≤50 participants) to £3,000 (≤30,000) verified State. Its real value is that AU/UK funders accept it
CompACT Psychological flexibility: Openness to Experience · Behavioural Awareness · Valued Action, 23 items Free for clinical and research use verified Self-perceived capability — and the three factors map almost exactly onto K-04's language
ERQ Habitual use of reappraisal and suppression Free claim Strategy-use frequency — the nearest self-report analogue to "reps." Doesn't measure skill quality
DERS Difficulties in emotion regulation Free claim Closest self-report to "able to do", but heavily deficit-worded
SDQ Emotional/conduct problems Free on paper for non-profits; electronic requires authorisation verified Deficit-framed — actively off-message

⚠ Do not use AAQ-II. verified Wolgast (2014, Behavior Therapy) argued it measures psychological distress, not psychological inflexibility; Tyndall et al. (2019) found it correlates more strongly with neuroticism and negative affect than with theoretically related acceptance processes — a discriminant validity failure.

inference This matters strategically beyond instrument selection: a state measure masquerading as a process measure is exactly the error MFC's entire positioning exists to name.

CompACT has short forms verified: CompACT-18, CompACT-15 (Hsu 2023, with demonstrated measurement invariance over time — critical for pre/post), CompACT-10, CompACT-8, and CompACT-Youth (Morey et al. 2024).

VIA Character Strengths

verified VIA-IS-R: 192 items, 8 per strength, 24 strengths under 6 virtues; higher internal consistency than the original VIA-IS (McGrath et al., 2022, Journal of Personality Assessment). Free to take. Used within the US Army's CSF/MRT alongside the Global Assessment Tool.

inference Verdict: a trait/self-concept measure, not a capability measure, and not sensitive to short-term change by design — strengths are conceived as stable. Useful as a free engagement and personalisation tool at program entry; useless as a pilot outcome. Do not present it as evidence.

inference Note also: CSF/MRT is the field's cautionary tale — a program at enormous scale whose evaluation was criticised for self-report-only outcomes and absent control groups. Citing it as precedent for scale is fine; citing it as precedent for evidence is not.

Observational

CLASS (Pianta et al.) — the primary observational outcome in RULER's trials. Observer training from ~US$100, certification requires a reliability test plus annual recertification; contract observers paid ~US$150–350 per observation verified.

inference Poor fit for MFC. CLASS measures the adult's environment, not the participant's capability. It is a proxy — exactly the substitution the field is criticised for. Also school-bound and observer-cost-heavy.

360 / informant report — inference underused and cheap. A single-item-per-skill rating from a manager, teacher, coach or peer ("in the last month, how often did X do Y?") triangulates self-report and is behavioural in reference. Weak psychometrics unless carefully developed, but strong face validity to funders. Worth including as a secondary measure.

⭐ The white space — and it is Australian and free

inference Three gaps, in descending order of how genuinely unfilled they are:

  1. No validated measure of skill enactment frequency in situ. Everything measures knowledge of what to do, belief about one's ability, or how one feels. Nobody measures how often, in real life, a person actually deployed a capability when an opportunity arose. That is exactly MFC's construct.
  2. No performance-based measure sensitive to short-term program change.
  3. No adult, Australian, capability-framed instrument.

Gap 1 is the one MFC can actually own — and the methodology to capture it already exists.

Ecological Momentary Assessment — the mechanism

verified EMA/ESM is repeated in-situ sampling, typically smartphone-delivered. Two modes: time-sampling (prompted several times daily) and event-sampling (participant self-initiates when a target event occurs).

Event-contingent sampling is the direct methodological analogue of a "mental rep."

It captures frequency, timing and context of behaviour free of retrospective recall bias, and within-person dynamics rather than between-person means. verified/inference

It is already established as a trial outcome measure verified: "Ecological Momentary Assessment as a Measure of Intervention Change: Evaluation in 4 Digital Mental Health Trials", JMIR 2025;27:e69297. It sets out the criteria EMA must meet to serve as a trial outcome — reliable, related-to-but-not-redundant-with conventional self-report, sensitive to intervention-related change, and associated with clinically relevant improvement. unknown — its actual findings and effect sizes were not retrievable. MFC must read the full text before citing numbers.

Platforms:

Platform Origin Cost
SEMA3 University of Melbourne (Melbourne School of Psychological Sciences + Melbourne eResearch Group) Free. Free iOS/Android apps; researcher access by request; published as Koval et al., Behavior Research Methods 56(7) verified
m-Path KU Leuven Free/academic claim
LifeData US commercial Subscription, priced by researchers/participants claim
Avicenna (ex-Ethica) Canada unknown

What an MFC rep-measure would look like

hypothesis — high confidence.

Event-contingent prompt: "Since the last prompt, did a moment come up where you had to [handle a strong feeling / say the hard thing / choose what matters]?" → if yes: "What did you do?" (fixed options mapped to MFC's taught skills, i.e. Stop-Shift-Do) → "How did it go?" (1–5).

Outputs: - Rep frequency per day/week - Skill-use rate — reps where a taught skill was deployed ÷ opportunities that arose - Latency from program to first unprompted rep - Maintenance at 4 / 8 / 12 weeks post-program

inference Opportunity-conditioned skill-use rate is a behavioural metric. It is not sentiment. It measures dose of practice in real life — which is literally SWM-03. No wellbeing-program evaluation found in this research is doing this as a primary outcome.

Note how close MFC already is. The Stage 10 forms already ask "did you attempt a mental rep in any of the three moments — even once?" and "did any of those moments come up at all, whether or not you tried a rep?" — that second item is already an opportunity denominator. MFC has invented the numerator and denominator of the right metric on paper. EMA turns a single retrospective question into a repeated in-the-moment count.

What it would take inference: ethics approval (needs a university or independent HREC partner), item development and cognitive pre-testing, a compliance plan (EMA compliance is the standard failure mode — budget for dropout and pre-register the threshold), and multilevel/within-person analysis capability. Realistically one academic co-investigator plus a statistician. Non-trivial but not expensive.

⚠ Reactivity caveat verified as a known issue: prompting someone about reps may itself increase reps. This is a genuine confound needing a design answer — EMA in both arms, or a delayed-EMA control.

Four options, with trade-offs

Option A — Off-the-shelf. Minimum risk, minimum contribution.

STEM-B (18 items, free) + CompACT-15 (free, time-invariant) + K10 (free, as a deliberate distress/safety contrast), pre/post. Cost near zero · credibility adequate · STEM-B is genuine capability, CompACT self-perceived capability, K10 the "we know the difference" control · contribution to the field: none · risk: small n on α≈.68 instruments may yield a null.

hypothesis This is the floor, not the plan.

Option B — Option A + event-contingent EMA on SEMA3. ⭐ Recommended.

Same battery, plus a 2–4 week SEMA3 event-contingent rep log spanning program and follow-up. SEMA3 is free; real costs are ethics, item development and analysis · credibility high — EMA is the methodologically prestigious move, and JMIR 2025 gives a citable framework for EMA-as-outcome · behavioural capability measurement · contribution genuine · risks: compliance attrition, reactivity, HREC required.

Option C — Commission a bespoke situational judgement test.

Partner with Carolyn MacCann's group at the University of Sydney (author of STEM/STEU) to build an MFC-aligned SJT. Cost unknown but SJT development is expensive — item generation, expert scoring panel, IRT validation, norming; likely six figures and 18–24 months. Highest credibility ceiling.

hypothesis Wrong sequencing. A charity with no pilot evidence should not build an instrument first. Position as Stage 2, funded off the back of Option B's results.

Option D — SWEMWBS only. The sector default.

£75 licence, universally accepted by funders, zero methodological effort.

inference Actively counterproductive. SWEMWBS measures mental health. Using it as the headline outcome concedes MFC's entire category argument. Include it as a secondary measure so funders get the number they recognise — but the primary must be a capability metric. This is the same critique that applies to the current WHO-5 choice.

The strategic recommendation

hypothesis Run Option B — and frame the measurement approach itself as a deliverable.

MFC's problem — no outcome evidence — inverts into an asset: it can design its first evaluation without legacy commitments to the wrong battery. The pitch to funders and academic partners is not "we ran a program and people liked it." It is:

The field concedes it has no performance-based, change-sensitive measure of emotional capability. We are building the first evaluation that measures skill enactment in real life, using free Australian-built EMA infrastructure, alongside the best available capability tests. Whether the program works or not, the measurement protocol is a contribution.**

That is a fundable proposition for a charity with zero evidence, and it is defensible to a methodologist. It also creates natural academic partnership hooks — Melbourne for SEMA3, Sydney for STEM/STEU — partnerships that supply the HREC pathway and the statistical capability MFC lacks internally.

Open items to close before committing

  • Full text and findings of JMIR 2025;27:e69297 (EMA sensitivity to intervention change) unknown — must be read
  • Whether STEM/STEU have published sensitivity-to-change evidence unknown
  • SEMA3 terms for a non-university organisation — the site is oriented to "researcher access"; a charity may need an academic sponsor unknown
  • MSCEIT 2 technical manual — norms, reliability, and whether scoring moved off consensus unknown
