11 Funding Regulation And Workforce

Funding channels, regulation, workforce and community models

Closes the six adjacent-field gaps flagged in the first pass. Three findings here are material enough to change decisions.

⚠ Three new "mental fitness" claimants — all Australian, all missed in the first pass

Fortem Australia — federally funded, uses the term as its organising word

verified fact Founded mid-2019, independent of employing agencies, serving first responders and their families. Registered charity, federally funded.

Uses "mental fitness" as its primary organising term. Its digital product is "Peak Fortem — a free online mental fitness toolkit for first responders and their families," hashtagged #MentalFitness. ANZMH describes it as "Free evidence-based mental fitness & wellbeing support for First Responders."

claim Scale: 25,250 first responders and family members supported · 3,690 social engagement activities across 340 local government areas · 10,245 clinical sessions · 2,040 Career Management Program participants.

Model — four legs: social connection activities (surfing, walks, coffee catch-ups, yoga) · psychology services · career management · mental health literacy.

inference Fortem is the clearest existing model of "mental fitness" built as an ecosystem: social activity is the front door, clinical service sits behind it. MFC's non-clinical red line means it can build leg one but must refer out for leg two — Fortem shows what a referral-partner architecture looks like.

But do not adopt their frame. Fortem's positioning is "bendable, not breakable" — a stress-inoculation frame appropriate to occupationally trauma-exposed populations. inference It quietly reimports the deficit model (how we are doing) that K-05 exists to escape. MFC's capability frame is genuinely more differentiated than Fortem's.

The Push-Up Challenge — the biggest single miss

verified fact Strapline: "Australia's largest physical and mental fitness event." Also "level up their mental fitness." Founded by Perth engineer Nick Hudson, 2017. Participants complete a push-up target over 24 days in June — the number marking lives lost to suicide in Australia.

⚠ Corrected 2026-08-06 after independent check. This previously stated a fixed 3,307 push-ups. The target is not fixed — it resets every year to the most recent published suicide toll. The 2025 Challenge was 3,214 push-ups, representing the 3,214 lives lost in 2023. verified fact File 17 carried the same error in a stronger form (claiming 3,307 "coincidentally" matched the 2024 toll) and has been corrected. Design consequence: the number MFC would be competing with moves annually — see file 18 on the "number that carries the message."

claim 2025: 234,000 participants · $12.8m raised · 33,000+ teams · 33,800 students, 785 schools. 2026: 230,000+ participants · $13m+ raised. Cumulative totals are unknown — the organisation's own page reported over $70m and over $80m at two research passes four days apart; do not publish either until one date-stamped capture exists. (Corrected 2026-08-06.) Beneficiaries: Lifeline, headspace, and its own Push for Better Foundation.

verified as absence No published outcome evidence. The impact page provides no outcome data and no independent evaluation.

strategic hypothesis This organisation has already done the thing MFC is trying to do — fuse the physical-fitness metaphor to mental wellbeing in the Australian public mind — reaching a quarter of a million Australians a year, with zero outcome evidence, in nine years.

It is simultaneously (a) proof the metaphor has enormous latent public appetite in Australia, (b) the largest existing occupant of MFC's language, and (c) a demonstration that in this category, distribution and ritual beat evidence for reach — but produce a fundraising vehicle, not a capability-building institution.

MFC's differentiator against it is precisely the lifelong-practice claim. The Push-Up Challenge is 24 days a year and routes money to crisis services — it is a fundraiser wearing the fitness metaphor, not a fitness program. That gap is MFC's opening, and MFC should be able to state it in one sentence.

Movember — Ahead of the Game

verified fact The AFL partnership is framed around improving "mental fitness" for young Australians and "harnessing the power of football to help build more mentally fit communities." claim Targets 60,000 participants in community football clubs; free; players and youth umpires 12–18 plus parents, coaches, volunteers.

claim Developed by researchers at the University of Wollongong; backed by a five-year international program of scientific evidence; described as "the only youth mental health literacy program endorsed in an evidence review commissioned by the AFL in 2020."

inference Movember shows the credible version of the metaphor: loose fitness language in marketing, tight literacy and resilience language in the program, and a university partner attached from the start. That is exactly the discipline K-08 should encode. Note the claim is a literacy outcome, not a wellbeing outcome — a precise, defensible boundary.

TGA regulation — a legal floor under the claims red lines

This converts K-08 from a brand and ethics position into a regulatory boundary with a specific statutory instrument.

verified fact Software meeting the medical device definition in s41BD of the Therapeutic Goods Act 1989 is regulated unless excluded. Exclusions sit in Schedule 1 of the Therapeutic Goods (Excluded Goods) Determination 2018 — currently 15 software categories.

Exclusion What it covers
Item 14B — general health or wellness software Software for general consumer use to promote or facilitate general health or wellness
Item 14E — digital mental health tool (conditional) Guidance published 16 March 2026

Item 14E's four conditions — all must be met claim, secondary source: 1. Intended to support users' mental health 2. Based on established clinical practice guidelines 3. Those guidelines clearly referenced 4. Guidelines accessible to the user inside the software itself

Falls outside 14E: novel or proprietary treatment approaches not yet recognised in Australian practice.

The trap specific to MFC

strategic hypothesis MFC's differentiator is that "mental fitness" is a new, proprietary category. Item 14E requires alignment with established clinical practice guidelines. So MFC's novelty disqualifies it from 14E.

MFC's software must therefore live in item 14B (general wellness) — or be registered on the ARTG. That makes the 14B boundary MFC's actual operating constraint, and makes "we are not treating anything" not merely a brand claim but the legal basis on which MFC could ship software without ARTG registration.

Where the line sits claim: software becomes a regulated device when it diagnoses, prevents or treats a disease, influences clinical decisions, or produces patient-specific outputs that guide care. Critically — "exclusion depends on intended purpose, claims, and how the software is used in practice, not just functionality."

inference The regulatory trigger is the claim, not the code. - Safe (14B): skill-building, practice logging, education, non-personalised content, no condition named, no symptom claim - Danger: any screening instrument (K10, PHQ-9, DASS) returning a personalised interpretation or severity band; any "you may be at risk of X" output; any triage logic acting on individual data

⚠ The sequencing risk: the moment MFC generates outcome evidence and starts saying "reduces distress", it may buy regulation with the same sentence that buys credibility.

unknown — TGA's own pages repeatedly timed out. Item numbers and the 14E conditions rest on TGA search-result text and a secondary legal source. Verify directly with the TGA before relying on this for any compliance decision. This is not legal advice.

Funding channels — a deflating but useful map

Health insurers: already allocated

Insurer Channel Open to MFC?
Bupa Foundation Community Grants Up to $10,000; 65 organisations shared >$600k in 2025; >$2m since 2019, for "mentally healthy and resilient communities" claim Yes — but small. Language fits MFC closely
Medibank Community Fund 1% of pre-tax profit; grants for healthy eating, physical activity, community connectedness claim Plausible — connectedness stream
Medibank Better Health Research Hub 2026: ~$695k across six partnerships incl. Orygen ($100k) and MCRI ($200k); streams include community mental health and wellbeing verified Not yet — requires a research-institute partner
HCF Research Foundation >$37.9m since 2000; 2026 priorities are acute need and health-services research verified No — MFC is neither
nib foundation "We no longer hold open grant rounds... we do not accept unsolicited requests" verified Closed

verified Who already occupies it: Lifeline (nib) · Black Dog + Kids Helpline (Bupa) · Orygen + MCRI (Medibank). All prior-research entities, on multi-year terms.

verified as absence No insurer uses "mental fitness." Medibank: "Live Better". Bupa: "mentally healthy". HCF: clinical service language.

hypothesis The insurer path is a two-step: win a small Bupa or Medibank community grant as a credibility marker, then co-apply with a university to the Medibank Better Health Research Hub — the only insurer channel that would actually fund the evidence MFC lacks.

Verdict: funding channel (minor), not a distribution channel. No evidence any insurer distributes third-party programs to members at scale.

Better-matched channels

  • Ian Potter Foundation — Community Wellbeing. Grants from $100,000, explicitly favouring preventative programs addressing root causes claim. hypothesis A better-matched funder than any health insurer, on both size and stated preference.
  • PHN commissioning — e.g. Healthy North Coast's Community Wellbeing Resilience Program claim. PHNs commission non-clinical wellbeing work — a channel absent from the first pass entirely.
  • Australia Post Community Grants — mental wellbeing and isolation claim.

The lived-experience workforce — the most directly usable precedent

verified fact National Lived Experience (Peer) Workforce Development Guidelines, National Mental Health Commission, launched December 2021 under Action 29 of the Fifth National Mental Health and Suicide Prevention Plan. Contains principles, values, roles and detailed steps for employers.

The workforce is framed as operating "from a human rights and social justice perspective rather than a medical perspective." verified fact

inference This is the single most useful precedent in the research for MFC's non-clinical positioning. It is the Commonwealth conceding, in writing, that a legitimate, funded, professional mental health workforce can be constituted on an explicitly non-medical basis. MFC does not have to invent that argument — it can cite it.

Credentialing verified fact: CHC43515 Certificate IV in Mental Health Peer Work — nationally recognised VET qualification, requires at least 80 hours of work placement, two streams (Consumer / Carer Peer Work). Delivered by RTOs including Mental Health Coordinating Council and RMIT. Its defining eligibility criterion is lived experience — the credential certifies experience plus training, not clinical competence.

Evidence — be honest about it verified fact: - Lloyd-Evans et al. (2014), systematic review and meta-analysis: 18 RCTs, 5,597 participants - Group peer support meta-analysis: 8 trials, 2,131 participants — small improvements to overall recovery, but not to hope or empowerment individually, and not to clinical symptoms - Youth anxiety/depression review: 9 RCTs, 2,003 participants — mixed; three showed no significant impact on depression

inference After two decades and dozens of RCTs, peer support shows small effects on recovery-type outcomes and largely null effects on clinical symptoms. A mature, funded, credentialed workforce that still cannot demonstrate large effects. That is both a warning and a permission structure.

What MFC should take

  1. A non-clinical workforce can be legitimised without becoming clinical — via three things MFC lacks: a recognised qualification, published role definitions and boundaries, and supervision structures. The peer workforce built all three between ~2012 and 2021.
  2. Scope-of-practice boundaries are the whole game. hypothesis MFC's realistic exposure is not that a workshop fails to help — it is that a facilitator without supervision mishandles a disclosure. The peer guidelines are a ready-made template to adapt rather than author. This bears directly on D-0016.
  3. A genuine fork in the road hypothesis: MFC could preference Cert IV Peer Work for facilitators — instant external legitimacy, but it imports the lived-experience-of-illness eligibility criterion, which conflicts with MFC's universal, non-deficit framing. Gyms do not require trainers to have been injured. This is a category-positioning decision disguised as an HR decision, and it should be made deliberately.
  4. Do not claim peer-support evidence as support for MFC. Those trials test peer support for people with diagnosed conditions in service settings — borrowing it would breach K-08.

Community and environment models — a different scaling curve

Scale Evidence
Australian Men's Shed Association 1,300+ sheds, 50,000+ men; ~$5.2m over two years plus $1m/yr National Shed Development Programme claim Barbagallo et al. 2023 and Foettinger et al. 2022 systematic reviews: associations with self-rated health and reduced isolation, but evidence "predominantly qualitative and subjective", mechanisms poorly theorised verified
The Man Walk Founded 2018; n=377 across 121 postcodes Peer-reviewed cross-sectional study, BMC Public Health 2026. 54% moderate-to-high loneliness. The paper notes that since 2018 no evidence had described participants or outcomes at all verified
Parkrun Free, weekly, permanent, volunteer-run Cross-sectional surveys (Grunseit et al.); no RCTs. Gendered pattern: women's gains linked to mental health, men's to community connectedness verified

AMSA's doctrine, quoted: "Men don't talk face to face, they talk shoulder to shoulder." verified fact inference The single most transferable sentence in this file — an empirically-grounded design constraint for adult male engagement, and the opposite of a circle-of-chairs workshop.

The uncomfortable lesson

inference Men's Sheds achieved 1,300+ sites, 50,000 men and ~$6m/year of Commonwealth funding on an evidence base that systematic reviews describe as non-robust and mostly qualitative. Scale and legitimacy were won by reach, sector organisation and policy alignment — not trial evidence.

hypothesis These are the closest Australian analogues to Iceland's Planet Youth, and they win differently than curricula do. Their unit of scale is a replicable local site with a fixed ritual, not a delivered session. Marginal cost per new site ≈ volunteer time. MFC's workshop model has marginal cost ≈ facilitator time — a fundamentally worse scaling curve.

Repetition beats content. Parkrun is the same event every Saturday for twenty years. The shed is a shed. None has curriculum depth; all have frequency, permanence and low entry cost.

If "mental fitness" is genuinely a lifelong practice, the fitness analogy demands a gym, not a seminar — a recurring environment people return to, not a workshop they attend once. This is the same conclusion Gotcha4Life's 8% gym-conversion failure points at from the other direction.

Do not imitate: their evidence practice (self-report, cross-sectional, self-selected, severe healthy-volunteer bias) — MFC enters a market where evidence scrutiny is now far higher than it was in 2007. Nor the demographic narrowness (55+, male), nor dependence on a single Commonwealth line item.

ADF and emergency services — the domestic CSF lineage

verified fact BattleSMART draws on cognitive behaviour therapy and attribution retraining; teaches arousal reduction plus adaptive cognitive coping across four domains: physical, thoughts, emotions, behaviours. It is one of five modules within Keep Your Mates Safe – Peer Support Program. ADF commenced efficacy trials with Dr Amy Adler, a principal evaluator of US Comprehensive Soldier Fitness. Published effectiveness results unknown.

inference ADF is the direct Australian descendant of the CSF tradition — universal, non-clinical, skills-based, delivered by trained non-clinicians into an existing institution. The closest doctrinal ancestor of what MFC describes.

claim NSW Ambulance Wellbeing Workshop — three days for operational staff; post-workshop surveys report 84% positive change in wellbeing.

inference Exactly the kind of number MFC will be tempted to generate and must not overclaim. Post-session self-report satisfaction, no control, no follow-up. Sophisticated funders read it as such.

Do not build the ADF/CSF universal-mandatory model — it depends on institutional compulsion MFC does not have, and the CSF literature is contested on effect sizes.

What this file changes

  1. Three more Australian "mental fitness" claimants — Fortem, The Push-Up Challenge, Movember/AFL. The Push-Up Challenge is the largest occupant of MFC's language in the country, at 234,000 participants a year, with no outcome evidence.
  2. K-08 now has a statutory floor — TGA item 14B, and the trap that MFC's own novelty forecloses item 14E.
  3. The insurer channel is largely closed; philanthropy and PHN commissioning are better matched.
  4. A Commonwealth-endorsed precedent for a non-clinical workforce exists — with credentialing, supervision and role-boundary templates MFC can adapt, and a live positioning fork over lived-experience eligibility.
  5. Community models scale on a better curve than workshops do — and the fitness analogy, taken seriously, points at a recurring environment rather than an event.

Named gaps

  • Full TGA item 14B and 14E condition text unknown — verify before any compliance decision
  • Published BattleSMART effectiveness results unknown
  • Fortem Australia's funding quantum and source unknown
  • HCF Research Foundation eligibility for non-university applicants unknown

12 Stop Shift Do Prior Art

Stop-Shift-Do, the Radar, and the access gap — a prior-art audit

This file is deliberately unflattering. MFC is better served by knowing precisely what is its own and what isn't. The verdict is that two of MFC's three signature elements are rediscoveries of well-established work, and one appears genuinely unclaimed.

Labels: verified · claim · inference · hypothesis · unknown.

The headline

Element Verdict
Stop, Shift, Do Not novel. At least six named protocols occupy the identical three-slot structure; two share the first word
The Radar Not novel — it is implementation intentions (Gollwitzer, 1993/1999), the best-evidenced planning intervention in social psychology. But a genuine under-researched variant sits inside it
The access gap Not novel as theory — it restates Tulving & Pearlstone (1966). Possibly novel as a public-programme organising principle
The outcome-independent rep ⭐ The strongest candidate. No program found that operationalises a countable practice unit defined by attempt rather than result

1. Stop-Shift-Do — the structure is a natural attractor, not an invention

verified Aligned by function:

Protocol Origin / date ① Interrupt ② Shift ③ Act Closeness
Stop, Shift, Do MFC Stop Shift Do —
DBT STOP Linehan, 1993 / 2015 Stop Take a step back · Observe Proceed mindfully 9/10
MBSR STOP Goldstein, 2012 (MBSR lineage 1979) Stop Take a breath · Observe Proceed 9/10
SBNRR Tan / Google Search Inside Yourself, 2012 Stop Breathe · Notice · Reflect Respond 9/10
Choice Point Harris, Bailey & Ciarrochi, ~2015 Notice the hook Name it a choice point Towards move 9/10 (framing)
Meta-Moment Brackett / Yale, ~2010s Sense the shift Pause · See best self Strategise & Act 8/10
ACE / drop anchor Harris, 2019 (ACT) (implicit) Acknowledge · Come back to body Engage 8/10
Reset routine Orlick / Boutcher, 1980s– (sport) Recognise Release Refocus on next action 8/10
PQ rep / intercept Chamine, 2012 Intercept Saboteur 10-sec sensory PQ rep Sage response 8/10
Real-time Resilience Reivich & Seligman, 2011 Catch the thought Evidence / reframe Counter-statement 6/10
HALT AA, mid-20th century Halt Check H/A/L/T Address the need 5/10

inference Two independent traditions — DBT and MBSR — converged on an identical four-step "STOP". That convergence is itself evidence the structure is a natural solution, not an invention. Dozens of unattributed three-step variants circulate in coaching and school SEL ("Pause, Breathe, Choose"; "Notice–Name–Navigate"). The three-slot structure is effectively public domain.

Note also that Brackett's step one is literally "sense the shift" — the shared vocabulary is not a coincidence in a crowded genre.

hypothesis Claiming Stop-Shift-Do as a model is a credibility liability that any clinician in the room will spot within thirty seconds. Treat it as a wording choice within a well-established genre, and cite the lineage explicitly — Linehan, Goldstein, Tan, Brackett, Harris.

On evidence, an important nuance verified: none of these protocols has standalone trial evidence. DBT's STOP sits inside an RCT-validated package; SBNRR and the Meta-Moment are components of evaluated approaches. The component being inside a validated program is not the same as the component being validated. MFC should not borrow their evidence either.

2. ⚠ The Radar is implementation intentions — the most important correction in this research

verified Pre-selecting specific everyday situations in advance in order to notice and act when they arise is implementation intentions (Gollwitzer, 1993, 1999). The mechanism Gollwitzer describes — pre-specifying a cue heightens that cue's perceptual accessibility and automates cue→response retrieval — is precisely what MFC claims the Radar does.

The evidence base is the strongest in this entire research programme: - Gollwitzer & Sheeran (2006) meta-analysis: 94 tests, d = 0.65 - Sheeran, Listrom & Gollwitzer (2024): 642 tests - Webb & Sheeran (2006): documents the intention–behaviour gap — intention change d=0.66 → behaviour change d=0.36 - WOOP/MCII (Oettingen) is the consumer-facing version — already free and already public

The genuine difference — narrow but real

Implementation intentions The Radar
What is pre-specified Cue and response — "if X, then I will do Y" Cue only — the response is left to in-moment judgement (Stop-Shift-Do)
What it targets A goal Practice volume, regardless of goal

hypothesis That "cue-specified, response-open" variant is genuinely under-researched. Gollwitzer's evidence is for fully specified plans. Whether cue-only pre-commitment retains the effect is an open empirical question. If MFC wants a research claim, that is it.

But MFC must stop describing the Radar as an original insight. It is a variant of the single most-cited planning intervention in psychology. Not citing Gollwitzer will look either uninformed or evasive.

inference This also has a practical upside: the recommendation elsewhere in this research to "add implementation intentions to the workshop close" is not an addition at all — it is closing the response slot that the Radar deliberately leaves open. MFC should decide knowingly whether to leave it open (novel, untested) or close it (proven, d=0.65). That is a real design decision, not a tweak.

3. The access gap — good translation of old science, not new science

verified Every component of the access framing already exists, and most of it is old:

Concept Source Relation to MFC's claim
Availability vs accessibility Tulving & Pearlstone (1966) The exact distinction, in those exact words, in memory research. Traces available in storage but inaccessible without a retrieval cue. MFC's core claim is a direct restatement of a 60-year-old finding, transposed to skills
Inert knowledge Whitehead (1929); Bransford & CTGV (1980s–90s) Knowledge "welded" to its learning context — expressible but unusable. The access gap, named in education a century ago
Learning vs performance Soderstrom & Bjork (2015) Performance is an unreliable index of learning
Intention–behaviour gap Sheeran (2002); Webb & Sheeran (2006) —
Knowing–doing gap Pfeffer & Sutton (2000) Organisational framing
Stress and executive function Arnsten (2009), Nature Reviews Neuroscience Even mild uncontrollable stress rapidly impairs PFC function while strengthening amygdala/striatal habit responses. The neuroscience of "skills you have but cannot reach"
Choking under pressure Beilock & Carr (2001); Beilock (2010) Working-memory hijack
Emotion regulation choice Sheppes, Scheibe, Suri & Gross (2011) The closest academic analogue to MFC's thesis — an established research programme on which strategy a person reaches for in the moment, and why
Regulatory flexibility Bonanno & Burton (2013) Context sensitivity, repertoire, feedback; rejects the "fallacy of uniform efficacy"

inference K-04's "access and coordinate relevant human skills across changing situations" is close to a paraphrase of Bonanno & Burton's regulatory flexibility, plus Sheppes' emotion-regulation choice.

Is it novel as an applied position?

verified ACT's psychological flexibility is fundamentally an access-not-possession model. DBT's distress-tolerance module exists precisely because skills degrade under arousal. Stress inoculation training (Meichenbaum, 1985) exists to make skills accessible under load.

But: inference no lay-facing public-health programme was found whose headline organising claim is "you already have the skills; the gap is access."

hypothesis MFC's framing is not new knowledge — it may be a new packaging position. A real but modest distinction. Presented uncited it reads as naive; presented cited it reads as sophisticated translation work — which is a legitimate and valuable contribution for a charity.

⚠ A seam critics will find quickly

inference K-04 lists "power, safety, environment, support" among the determinants of access — a structural/social-determinants claim. But the intervention is purely individual: reps at pre-chosen moments.

Either the model addresses environmental access, or the framing should be narrowed. This is the same seam the individualisation critique attacks (see [[60-projects/market-and-competitor-intelligence-v1/01-category-language-and-positioning-risk|01]]) and the same one the WHS hierarchy-of-controls exposes (see [[60-projects/market-and-competitor-intelligence-v1/06-adjacent-fields-and-structural-forces|06]]). Three separate lines of attack converge on one unresolved design tension.

4. ⭐ The outcome-independent rep — the one genuinely unclaimed thing

"A mental rep is catching a moment and choosing your next move, on purpose, toward what matters... The outcome does not determine whether it counts."

inference Close cousins exist — ACT's process-over-outcome and "towards moves"; Bjork's learning-vs-performance; Dweck's process praise. But no program was found that operationalises a countable practice unit defined explicitly by attempt rather than result.

Fitness reps are counted exactly this way — which is why the metaphor works.

hypothesis If MFC plants a flag in one thing, it should be this: a measurable, outcome-independent unit of emotional-skill practice.

It is teachable, it is falsifiable, and it makes a research programme possible — rep count becomes an exposure variable. Nobody appears to own it.

This connects directly to [[60-projects/market-and-competitor-intelligence-v1/10-measurement-white-space|10 — Measurement white space]]: the unclaimed construct and the unclaimed measure are the same asset viewed from two sides.

5. ⚠ Two collisions MFC needs to know about

Positive Intelligence already owns "mental fitness" + "reps"

verified Shirzad Chamine's Positive Intelligence (2012) — tagline "Building mental fitness for all" — has a unit of practice literally called a "PQ rep": a 10-second sensory attention exercise, inside a "mental fitness" brand with "brain muscles" framing. Stanford-affiliated, NYT bestseller, sold at scale.

inference "Mental fitness / train the mind like a muscle / mental reps" is not available territory. Chamine got there in 2012. This is the most awkward finding in this file and it is not about Stop-Shift-Do at all.

verified A name collision also exists: "Mental Fitness Collective" is used by a Canadian/US wellness network (resolutelc.ca/mental-fitness-collective).

⚠ The published/internal divergence — verified directly, and worse than reported

A-17 verified this against mentalfitnesscollective.com.au directly on 2026-08-01, because the finding bears on MFC's own controlled records. There is a three-way divergence:

Source Definition of mental fitness
K-04 — locked 20 July 2026 "Mental fitness is how well we navigate life's everyday moments."
Public website verified "how well we can think, feel, and act so we can thrive, overcome challenges, adapt to change, and connect with others"
Internal framework The access-gap formulation — "a developable capacity to access and coordinate relevant human skills across changing situations"

The public site carries neither the locked kernel definition nor the internal evidence-facing one. This is a live instance of C-13, and it is on the public record rather than in a draft document.

Further, verified on the public site verified: - No mention of "Radar", "Stop, Shift, Do", or the access framing. - It presents seven core skills — self-awareness, self-regulation, flexible thinking, attention and focus, self-compassion, strengthening connections, purposeful action — described as "developed in collaboration with professionals in neuroscience, psychology, counselling and high performance sports coaching." (Note: Stage 10 explicitly excluded "the seven deeper skills or Human Operating System" as required content — so the public site is running ahead of the approved workshop package.) - Mental Fitness Month runs the "Daily 1% Model": 14 minutes a day across breathwork, mindfulness, gratitude, connection and visualisation.

🛑 A direct contradiction with the locked kernel

verified The public site frames mental fitness as "mental muscles" — "think about it like mental muscles, with Mental Reps used to build mental muscles that grow into skills."

K-04 states, verbatim: "The comparison is explanatory, not literal: the mind is not a muscle, and practice does not solve every problem."

The public site asserts as its central explanatory device the precise analogy the locked kernel prohibits taking literally. inference This is not a nuance — it is the difference between an explanatory comparison and a mechanistic claim, and it is the seam K-08 exists to protect. Recommend routing to A-05 as a controlled-record conflict, and to A-12 on claims.

Why the divergence matters strategically

inference The sophisticated access-gap framing is internal doctrine; the public artefact is a conventional daily-practice challenge.

The risk runs both ways: the distinctive part isn't published, and the published part is the least distinctive part. A 14-minutes-a-day, five-modality challenge sits very close to what Smiling Mind, the Push-Up Challenge and Positive Intelligence already offer — and "mental muscles + reps" is Chamine's exact territory since 2012. The thing that would actually differentiate MFC is sitting in the vault.

The verdict, stated plainly

Unflattering version: Stop-Shift-Do is a rediscovery, and a crowded one. The Radar is implementation intentions with the response slot left open. The access gap is a good translation of old science, not new science. The one thing that looks genuinely unclaimed is the outcome-independent rep.

hypothesis MFC's most credible strategy is to stop positioning as inventor and position as translator and aggregator — "we take five well-evidenced mechanisms and make them practiceable for people who will never see a therapist" — while doing original work on the rep as a measurable unit.

That is a defensible, fundable, honest position. The current implicit claim of novelty is not.

What this changes

  1. Cite the lineage. Linehan, Goldstein, Tan, Brackett, Harris for the loop. Gollwitzer for the Radar. Tulving, Bransford, Sheppes, Bonanno & Burton, Arnsten for the access gap. Citing raises credibility; omitting invites the charge of either ignorance or evasion.
  2. Decide the Radar's response slot knowingly — open (novel, untested) or closed (proven, d=0.65).
  3. Resolve the structural/individual seam in K-04, or narrow the framing.
  4. Plant the flag on the outcome-independent rep, and build the measure for it.
  5. Publish the good stuff. The differentiating framework is not on the public site.
  6. Get advice on the Positive Intelligence overlap before leaning further on "mental fitness + reps."

unknown — whether "Stop, Shift, Do" or "Radar" is trademarked or trademarkable given the density of prior use; whether any funder's due diligence has already flagged the Positive Intelligence overlap.

13 Category Coherence

Category coherence — the word is taken, the category is vacant

Hunter's hypothesis was that the term is used but the category has gaps and inconsistencies. That is confirmed, and understated. This file reframes the entire strategic finding of this research.

The headline

"Mental fitness" is not a coherent category. It is a loose family of usages sharing a word — with one orphaned Australian peer-reviewed construct sitting underneath it that almost nobody cites.

Six incompatible definitions of what kind of thing it is. A founding principle most users violate. No validated measure. And six of the highest-profile Australian users — including Black Dog Institute — never define it at all.

⭐ The find: an orphaned Australian consensus definition

Robinson, P., Oades, L. G., & Caputi, P. (2015). "Conceptualising and measuring mental fitness: A Delphi study." International Journal of Wellbeing, 5(1), 53–73. verified fact — full text retrieved and read.

An international expert panel (n=25), Delphi method, peer-reviewed, Australian. Its stated purpose is precisely MFC's problem:

"Despite the increased use of the term mental fitness... there is little consensus in relation to theory, definition and measurement. The concept of mental fitness could be used to parsimoniously engage, educate and promote proactive, positive mental health activities to the wider community, without stigma and within a language that is easily understood."

The consensus definition:

"Mental fitness is the modifiable capacity to utilise resources and skills to flexibly adapt to challenges or advantages, enabling thriving."

The four guiding principles verified: 1. "fitness is a positive term without connotations of illness implied by mental health or mental illness" 2. "mental fitness could be understood by the wider community in a similar way to physical fitness" 3. "mental fitness is measurable" 4. "mental fitness can be improved, in a similar way to physical fitness"

⚠ MFC has independently converged on this definition
Robinson et al. (2015) "the modifiable capacity to utilise resources and skills to flexibly adapt to challenges... enabling thriving"
K-04 evidence definition "a developable capacity to access and coordinate relevant human skills across changing situations"

inference These are close to the same sentence. MFC arrived independently at the peer-reviewed expert-consensus definition of its own category.

This is the single most useful fact in this research. It converts MFC's position from "we assert a definition" to "we adopt and complete the published expert-consensus definition" — at zero cost, with immediate academic standing, and with an obvious Australian partnership hook.

The provenance nobody in the sector knows

verified fact The term is not new. McCarthy (1964) proposed "mental fitness" to the APA's Committee on Mental Health Research Programs as a replacement for Knutson's (1963) "positive mental health" — which Knutson described as "left on the doorstep of the public and professional community as a neglected and starving stepchild." McCarthy asked the Committee "to try it on for size and see how well it fits."

The category has been available and unclaimed for sixty years.

The sharpest boundary statement in the literature — and it is unadopted

From the expert panel's recorded commentary verified:

"mental fitness should be focusing on the process while [mental health] should focus on the outcome."

inference One sentence that resolves the largest inconsistency in the entire category. It has expert-consensus provenance, it is published, and no organisation uses it. It is also a sharper version of what K-05 is reaching for.

What the panel itself objected to — these are the fault lines

verified — and they are MFC's inherited problems too: - Measurement: "I think it would be useful to operationalize exactly what you mean by strength, flexibility, and endurance" - Self-report: "care needs to be taken with whether it is measurable through self-report... this is a major problem with the VIA — what does self-reported sense of humour actually mean?" The panel recommended an objective measure. - Positive-only framing: "only focusing on the positive poll is neither scientifically justifiable or logical" - ⚠ Workplace hazard: "I would be concerned about passing judgement or discussing the mental fitness of employees" — a discrimination and legality risk flagged by the panel itself. This connects directly to the WHS findings in [[60-projects/market-and-competitor-intelligence-v1/06-adjacent-fields-and-structural-forces|06]]. - Where the analogy breaks: "Could an older person be physically challenged but still mentally well, or could a younger person be very fit but depressed?"

The rival operationalisation

verified Iorfino et al. (2024), npj Mental Health Research — "Quantifying the interrelationships between physical, social, and cognitive-emotional components of mental fitness using digital technology." Defines mental fitness as "our ability to think, feel, and act to achieve what we want in our daily lives." Operationalised via a 26-item Innowell questionnaire, n = 4,901 Australian adults, seven domains: physical activity, sleep/circadian, nutrition, substance use, daily activities, social connection, psychological distress.

inference Better measured, conceptually thinner — it measures lifestyle plus distress, not Robinson's capacity construct. Australian, well-powered, recent, and quietly staking a rival claim. Deserves a dedicated read.

unknown — Robinson's 2014 UOW thesis reportedly developed a measure, but the repository returned 403 and no peer-reviewed validation paper was located. Treat "a validated mental fitness scale exists" as unproven.

The incoherence, itemised

Six incompatible answers to "what kind of thing is it?"

Ontological category Who
Capacity Robinson et al. · Mental Fitness Australia · Iorfino et al.
Practice / process BetterUp ("a proactive practice") · Headversity · Smiling Mind (implicitly)
Habits Gotcha4Life ("adopting healthy habits") · MensLine
Skills Smiling Mind · MindUP
Performance outcome Danny Frawley Centre ("perform at our best") · Smiling Mind
Score Positive Intelligence (PQ 0–100) · Total Brain
Undefined branding token Push-Up Challenge · Fortem · AIS · Black Dog · Movember

A capacity, a practice, a habit set, a skill set, an outcome and a score are not the same kind of object and cannot share a definition. Note especially that Danny Frawley and Smiling Mind define it as the outcome — precisely the confusion the expert panel warned against.

🛑 Six prominent users never define it

verified — page-level:

  1. The Push-Up Challenge — "Australia's largest physical and mental fitness event", and that is the entire content
  2. AIS Mental Fitness Program — the term is in the program's name
  3. Black Dog Institute — Australia's most credentialled mental health research institute, co-delivering a program called "Mental Fitness", with no definition on the program page
  4. Fortem Australia — "Peak Fortem: Mental Fitness"
  5. Movember Ahead of the Game — "build mental fitness" as a stated outcome, undefined
  6. Gotcha4Life's flagship site — defined only on the Gym subdomain, not the main About page

inference Black Dog's involvement is the strategic crux: the term is being lent scientific credibility by association without being given scientific content.

The euphemism problem

inference, strongly evidenced. The fitness framing was invented (McCarthy 1964, ratified by Robinson's Principle 1) precisely as a non-stigmatising re-label for positive mental health.

The sector has kept the stigma-avoidance function and discarded the conceptual content.

  • MensLine conflates outright: "It's another way of taking care of yourself and your mental health." The definition is mental health care, renamed.
  • The Push-Up Challenge is a mental health fundraiser — its facts are about suicide — branded a "physical and mental fitness event."
  • AIS/Black Dog's stated purpose is to "improve mental health and wellbeing."

"Mental fitness" is currently, in majority practice, a euphemism with a research paper attached that nobody cites.

Prevention vs performance — an unreconciled split

Prevention-framed: MensLine · Smiling Mind · Gotcha4Life · MindUP · Push-Up Challenge Performance-framed: Danny Frawley · BetterUp · Positive Intelligence · Fortem ("Peak State") · CSF Both, unreconciled: Smiling Mind · Robinson ("enabling thriving")

verified These carry entirely different evidence burdens. A prevention claim requires longitudinal incidence data; a performance claim requires task-outcome data. No organisation in this audit distinguishes which claim it is making, and none presents evidence matched to the claim it makes.

The sector's largest unguarded flank — and MFC's largest reputational risk if it repeats the pattern. Directly relevant to K-08.

Near-total individualisation

Purely individual: Robinson · BetterUp · Positive Intelligence · Total Brain · MindUP · Mental Fitness Australia · MensLine Gestures at relationships: Gotcha4Life alone ("connect with others", "meaningful mateship") Includes environment/institution: effectively nobody

inference The construct as it stands makes mental fitness a personal responsibility and is silent on conditions. This is the exact point at which the physical-fitness analogy becomes politically loaded — and it is the same seam identified in [[60-projects/market-and-competitor-intelligence-v1/12-stop-shift-do-prior-art|12]] and [[60-projects/market-and-competitor-intelligence-v1/06-adjacent-fields-and-structural-forces|06]]. Three independent analyses now converge on it.

No validated measure exists

Status
Robinson et al. Principle 3 asserts measurability. Never delivered as a validated instrument. Panel rejected the operationalisation as under-specified
Iorfino et al. 2024 The strongest actual measurement — but measures lifestyle + distress, not the capacity construct
Positive Intelligence PQ 0–100, proprietary, no independent validation located
Total Brain Mental Health Index — the name concedes the boundary
BetterUp No "Mental Fitness Index" exists — despite marketing itself as the world's largest mental fitness company
Everyone else Nothing

The field asserts measurability far more than it demonstrates it. This is the same conclusion reached independently in [[60-projects/market-and-competitor-intelligence-v1/10-measurement-white-space|10]].

The analogy is load-bearing and unexamined

verified Smiling Mind is the only practitioner organisation found to disclaim it: "Mental fitness doesn't literally mean the brain is a muscle that can be worked out."

inference Where it breaks: physical fitness has objective, non-self-report measures (VO₂max, 1RM); mental fitness has none. Physical fitness has established dose-response protocols; mental fitness has none. Physical fitness does not predict its mental analogue.

Note K-04 already contains the correct disclaimer — "the mind is not a muscle" — putting MFC ahead of every organisation here except Smiling Mind. But MFC's own public site currently violates it. See [[60-projects/market-and-competitor-intelligence-v1/12-stop-shift-do-prior-art|12]].

The strategic reframe

The word is taken. The category is vacant.

This is a materially better position than the one recorded in [[60-projects/market-and-competitor-intelligence-v1/01-category-language-and-positioning-risk|01]], and it supersedes it.

Why the conditions are unusually favourable strategic hypothesis:

  1. The term has mass public traction and zero definitional ownership
  2. The biggest incumbents — Black Dog, AIS, Push-Up Challenge, Fortem, Movember — have declined to define it. Claiming the definition takes nothing from them and can be framed as a service to them
  3. An Australian, peer-reviewed, expert-consensus definition already exists and is orphaned. MFC does not need to invent — only to complete, adopt and steward
  4. The highest-value gap (measurement) is precisely the gap the original authors flagged and never closed — and MFC's outcome-independent rep plus EMA is a credible way to close it

The risks, stated plainly: - Definitional leadership without an instrument is just another opinion — the sector already has twelve - The panel's workplace hazard is real: judging individuals' "mental fitness" in employment settings carries discrimination and legality risk. A collective/environmental dimension is not merely intellectually superior — it is protective

The fool's-errand version is a nice framework on a website. The real version is: definition + validated measure + free framework + adoption by others.

How CASEL actually did it — the playbook

verified The right comparator, and the mechanism is legible:

  1. A convening, not a publication. Both the term "social and emotional learning" and CASEL itself were born at a single 1994 gathering at the Fetzer Institute — researchers, educators and child-development experts convened expressly "to create a coherent framework and common vocabulary." The definition emerged from a room, not a paper.
  2. Codify fast, in practitioner-usable form. Within three years: Promoting Social and Emotional Learning: Guidelines for Educators (1997) — the document that formally defined the field. Not a journal article: a practitioner guide.
  3. A small, memorable, countable framework. The CASEL 5 — and note it includes relational and social competencies, not only intrapersonal ones.
  4. Give it away. CASEL owns the framework by making it free and universally citable. Ownership came from adoption, not licensing — the opposite of the Positive Intelligence and MTQ48 commercial-instrument model, which buys revenue at the cost of category leadership.
  5. Be the evidence infrastructure. CASEL's authority rests on programme reviews and meta-analysis, which made it the arbiter of what counts.
  6. Hold the boundary in public.

The MFC translation strategic hypothesis

CASEL move MFC equivalent
The 1994 Fetzer convening Convene Robinson, Oades, Black Dog, Smiling Mind, Gotcha4Life, AIS, Movember, Push-Up Challenge to ratify one definition. Robinson's 2015 Delphi is the pre-read
The 1997 practitioner guide A free, practitioner-usable mental fitness framework — with a collective dimension built in from day one, which would differentiate it from every definition in this audit
The CASEL 5 A small, nameable, countable competency set
Give it away Free and universally citable. Not licensed
Evidence infrastructure Complete and openly publish the validated instrument the field has promised since 1964. Whoever publishes the measure owns the construct — the single highest-leverage action available
Hold the boundary Adopt the panel's unclaimed sentence: mental fitness is the process; mental health and wellbeing are the outcomes

What this changes in the record

  • SWM-02 should not simply be downgraded. The claim "MFC is defining mental fitness as a category" is wrong as stated — but "MFC is completing and stewarding an unfinished, published, Australian expert-consensus definition" is both accurate and a stronger position. Recommend rewriting rather than weakening. See [[60-projects/market-and-competitor-intelligence-v1/08-strategic-world-model-contradictions|08]].
  • K-04's evidence-facing definition should cite Robinson et al. (2015). It is nearly the same sentence, and citation converts assertion into adoption.
  • K-05 has a sharper published cousin — process vs outcome — worth considering alongside how we are doing / what we are able to do.
  • K-08 gains a specific requirement: distinguish prevention claims from performance claims, and match evidence to whichever is being made. No organisation in the category does this.

Open items

  • Robinson's 2014 UOW thesis — does it contain a validated scale? Repository returned 403 unknown
  • Iorfino et al. (2024) — dedicated read required; it is the live rival operationalisation unknown
  • Whether BetterUp holds an internal unpublished index unknown
  • Second pass on Fortem, Movember and Black Dog sub-pages before publishing the "never defines it" claim externally

14 Movember And Mens Cluster

Movember and the Australian men's mental-health cluster — full profiles

Seven organisations. One of them is the largest men's-health funder on earth and is headquartered 20 minutes from MFC's likely delivery footprint.

Every claim below is labelled: verified fact · public organisational claim · inference · strategic hypothesis · unknown. Marketing copy is never recorded as verified fact. No number in this file is estimated. Where a figure could not be verified it is written unknown with a note on what would verify it. Where two true facts could be stitched into a causal claim, they are kept apart and the join is flagged.

MC-01 — MOVEMBER (primary)

Relationship to MFC funder / category-language competitor / potential partner — all three at once

The headline correction

⚠ REVISION to file 01's weight — NOT a correction to file 13. File 01 rates Movember's use of "mental fitness" as "Medium–high"; file 13 lists it among incumbents who "have declined to define it." File 01's register entry is correct and already records this usage — only its weight requires revision. File 13's entry should NOT be changed on this evidence. As at 2026-08-06:

⚠ Corrected 2026-08-06 after independent check. This section originally concluded that Movember had "renamed its mental-health content category to 'mental fitness' globally" and was "the third definitional 'mental fitness' claimant in Australia," at "Very high" weight, and pushed corrections into files 01 and 13. The independent check reproduced the redirect evidence exactly — it is real — but found the conclusion drawn from it unsupported. The FY25 annual report full text uses "mental health" 35 times and "mental fitness" 5 times verified fact, and in the same paragraphs describes Movember as "the official mental health partner" to BLAST. The single page carrying a "definition" is the New Zealand locale, whose own <title> remains "Men's mental health. Let's talk about it. | Movember", with "MENTAL FITNESS RESOURCES" appearing as a section heading, not a category name. And "in Australia" is falsified by this file's own finding — an Australian user gets a 404. A one-sentence marketing gloss on one locale, with no construct boundary, no measure and no exclusion, is not a definition in the sense file 13 means.

  • verified fact Every Movember locale's mental-health page 301-redirects to /mental-fitness. Verified by direct HTTP header inspection, 2026-08-06, and independently reproduced by the checker: au|us|uk|ca|ie|nz.movember.com/mens-health/mental-health and /about/mental-health all → https://movember.com/mental-fitness → https://au.movember.com/mental-fitness. Movember has migrated its mental-health URL slug to /mental-fitness globally. inference What this signals about intent is genuine and worth watching; it is not by itself a category claim.
  • verified fact The FY25 Annual Report calls Movember Ahead of the Game "our flagship youth mental fitness program"; says Movember is "backing programs that embed mental fitness into sport"; and describes "embedding mental fitness directly into the esports ecosystem" via the BLAST partnership.
  • verified fact A definition now exists on the live page: "Mental fitness isn't just about getting through the tough times. It's about building the resilience to handle whatever life throws at you." (nz.movember.com/mental-fitness, accessed 2026-08-06.)
  • verified fact The AU and US/UK/CA/IE /mental-fitness URLs currently return HTTP 404 — the redirect target is broken in five of six locales; only nz.movember.com/mental-fitness returns 200. inference This is a mid-migration state, not a retreat: you do not point six locales' canonical mental-health URLs at a path you are abandoning.

Revised weight: High (from "Medium–high") — not "Very high," and not "definitional." strategic hypothesis The defensible statement: Movember has migrated its mental-health URL slug to /mental-fitness across all six locales and uses the term five times in its FY25 report, including for its flagship youth programme — but its own reporting language, page titles and partnership descriptions remain "mental health," and the Australian /mental-fitness URL currently 404s.

Movember is a watch-list category entrant with the deepest pockets in the sector, not an established definitional claimant. It does not join Gotcha4Life and Smiling Mind as a third definitional claimant on this evidence. What would change that verdict, and should be re-checked in ~90 days: the AU /mental-fitness URL returning 200 with a substantive page; "mental fitness" overtaking "mental health" in an annual report; or a published construct definition with a boundary and a measure.

What they do

Movember is primarily a funder and evidence-builder, secondarily a direct deliverer. inference — strongly supported by the FY25 financial structure below and by its own stated model.

Its own four-part description of how it works: Fund Bold Solutions · Train the Frontline · Influence Systems · Share What Works. verified fact (FY25 report). Three change levels are named: Individuals · Norms · Systems. verified fact

The Movember Institute of Men's Health — launched 2023 with an AUD $100 million commitment; Global Director Professor Simon Rice. verified fact (FY25 report). It is the research/policy engine: convening, advocacy, evidence-building, real-world delivery.

That combined biomedical research with survivorship and health outcomes under the word "research," inflating the research line more than sevenfold. The corrected split actually strengthens the point being made: the thing Movember is popularly understood to fund — cancer research — is 4.2% of program expenditure, against 43.2% for mental health and suicide prevention.

The presentation point, stated carefully. verified fact The report displays a 78.9% / 15.8% / 5.3% split. verified (arithmetic): fundraising expenditure is 15.82% of revenue and administration 5.29% of revenue — so the 78.9% "programs" figure is the residual (100 − 15.8 − 5.3), not actual program expenditure. Actual program expenditure was 64.3% of FY25 revenue. The gap is the $20.2m surplus, which Note 2 explains as timing — "a difference between the timing of funds raised and the associated program expenditure outflows, which will occur in future years."

inference This is a defensible accounting explanation, not a misstatement — but the pie chart a reader sees says 78.9% and the cash that actually moved to programs was 64.3%. MFC should note the technique rather than adopt it.

Movember Conversations is built on R U OK?'s ALEC framework (Ask, Listen, Encourage action, Check in). verified fact inference This is a significant ecosystem fact: the largest men's-health funder in the world adopted a small Australian campaign charity's four-step protocol as the spine of its own global digital product rather than authoring one. It is direct evidence for file 02's recommendation that MFC needs an ALEC-equivalent — a sayable, teachable protocol travels further than an organisation does.

The "social connection" thesis

public organisational claim Movember's Real Face of Men's Health report series pushes social disconnection and loneliness as a primary, actionable driver of men's poor health outcomes. Reported findings include: one in four UK men aged 15–34 frequently experience loneliness; 38% of men vs 54% of women would seek emotional support from friends; 71% agree a bigger discussion of male loneliness is needed; 50% of the Irish public believe young men are becoming increasingly disconnected. public organisational claim — these are Movember's own survey figures; the underlying instruments, sampling frames and n's were not verified in this pass unknown.

verified fact The thesis is also embedded structurally: the Indigenous portfolio is explicitly built to strengthen "the cultural, spiritual, and social connections that keep men well"; the sport strategy is framed as turning "the game into a force for connection"; the gaming study is designed around "the connection fostered through play."

⚠ Do not stitch. Movember publishes (a) loneliness prevalence data and (b) a portfolio of connection-building programs. It has not published evidence that its programs reduce loneliness or that reduced loneliness caused any health outcome it reports. Those are two true facts and a missing middle. MFC must not repeat the join, and should expect Movember's marketing to imply it.

strategic hypothesis Social connection is the strategic ground Movember is claiming, and it is adjacent to — not identical with — MFC's ground. Movember's claim is men are disconnected; rebuild the connections. MFC's claim is mental fitness is a trainable capability. A connection thesis is an environment thesis; a fitness thesis is a practice thesis. They are compatible, which makes Movember a more plausible eventual funder than an eventual competitor — but the "mental fitness" URL migration means the language collision is real regardless.

Evidence base — forensic

This is the strongest and most honestly published evidence base of any organisation in this report set, and it still does not show what the marketing says it shows.

MAOTG primary trial verified fact:

Vella, S.A., Swann, C., Batterham, M., et al. (2021). "An Intervention for Mental Health Literacy and Resilience in Organized Sports." Medicine and Science in Sports and Exercise. Design: controlled, non-randomised (per the 2018 protocol, which itself names "self-selection bias and non-randomised design" as risks). Sample: 350 intervention, 466 control adolescent males. Significant positive group×time interactions: depression and anxiety literacy · intentions to seek help from formal sources · confidence to seek mental health information · resilience. NO group×time interaction (null results): social distance (stigma) · intentions to seek help from informal sources · implicit beliefs about adversity.

Health economic evaluation verified fact:

Eckermann, S., McCaffrey, N., Tonmukayakul, U., Swann, C., Vella, S. (2021). Health Economics Review. 343 intervention / 273 control. "Mean incremental effects favoured AOTG in all dimensions (10/13 significantly at 5% level)." Implementation cost conservatively estimated at $37.47 per participant.

Process evaluation verified fact: Vella et al., Journal of Applied Sport Psychology, 2025 — underlying mechanisms of the intervention.

⚠ Discrepancy, flagged. The FY25 Annual Report states: "Peer-reviewed studies show the program reduces psychological distress and improves mental wellbeing outcomes." The primary trial's reported significant outcomes are literacy, help-seeking intentions, confidence and resilience — not psychological distress. A search of Europe PMC (2026-08-06) did not locate a peer-reviewed paper reporting reduced psychological distress as a significant MAOTG outcome. inference Either such a paper exists and was not surfaced by this search, or the annual-report sentence is a summary that outruns the published record. unknown — what would resolve it: a citation list from Movember for that specific sentence.

This is precisely the K-08 failure mode, committed by the most sophisticated organisation in the category. It is the strongest available argument for MFC binding its own claims to named papers and named outcomes.

Family Man verified fact: Movember's own publications page lists no standalone efficacy trial of Family Man. The cited evidence is for predecessor programs — ParentWorks (Piotrowska et al., Child Psychiatry and Human Development) and AccessEI (Dadds et al., Journal of Consulting and Clinical Psychology, 2019, 87, 706–719, two RCTs).

inference This is the same structure as The Resilience Project's evidence page (file 02): evidence for the ingredients and the ancestors, not for the shipped product. That Movember does it too is important — it means the pattern is a category norm, not one competitor's sloppiness, and MFC's differentiation on this axis is available against the whole field.

Movember Conversations verified fact: Erskine, K. & Healey, M. (2022), "Conversations that count: Lessons from evaluating a men's digital mental health response during COVID-19," Evaluation Journal of Australasia. This is a methods/lessons paper about evaluation design during a product pivot — not an outcome evaluation. inference Movember's most publicly-visible mental health product has no published outcome evidence.

The sector-level finding — the single most useful evidence fact in this file verified fact:

Slade, A., Reily, N.M., Fujimoto, H., Seidler, Z.E., Christensen, H., Shand, F., Tang, S. (2025). "Men's mental health and suicide prevention service landscape in Australia: a scoping review." BMC Public Health 25(1). Funded by the Medical Research Future Fund (grant 1200195). Zac Seidler is affiliated with the Movember Institute of Men's Health, Orygen and University of Melbourne; the other six authors are Black Dog Institute / UNSW. 88 Australian services and initiatives identified for men at suicide risk. 84.1% offer awareness and education. Only 22.7% have any formal evaluation. Only three used a randomised controlled trial.

inference Four out of five men's suicide-prevention services in Australia do awareness and education; fewer than one in four has ever been evaluated; three in the entire country have RCT evidence. This is the market MFC is entering, described by its own most credible participants. It is simultaneously the bar (low) and the opportunity (an evaluated program is genuinely rare).

Brand and fundraising engine

verified fact FY25: 291,053 registered participants globally, generating AUD $138.4m. verified (computed): $475.49 raised per registered participant.

verified fact The engine is: an owned annual calendar moment (November) + a physical, visible, socially-legible act (growing a moustache) + peer-to-peer sponsorship + corporate partners (L'Oréal, Gillette, Amazon, Pringles, lululemon) + stunt-driven earned media.

inference Movember, R U OK?Day and The Push-Up Challenge all run the same machine: a fixed annual date, a simple physical/social act, peer sponsorship. This is now three independent proofs that the calendar-anchor model is the dominant fundraising architecture in Australian men's mental health. File 02 already recommended MFC create a calendar anchor; this file raises that from a good idea to the observed sector default.

Policy engine — the FY25 breakthrough, and where the money went

verified fact Ahead of the 2025 Australian federal election Movember ran its first Election Platform. Both major parties committed to men's health outcomes. A $32.0m federal pledge followed — described in the FY25 report as the largest federal investment in men's health on record. Allocation:

Recipient Amount Purpose
Movember $18.7m Scale Men in Mind and Movember Ahead of the Game
Australian Men's Shed Association $8.3m Expand National Shed Development Program + new health promotion
Healthy Male $3.0m Plus Paternal — fatherhood preparation and parenting skills
Black Dog Institute $2.0m Spud's Game at the Danny Frawley Centre

verified fact Separately, $11.3m in federal funding in FY25 for gender-responsive training across general practice, pharmacy and nursing.

strategic hypothesis This is the most strategically significant fact in this file for MFC. Movember did not merely win a grant — it wrote the men's-health line item and then distributed it to the rest of the sector. AMSA's own 2025 Chairman's Report credits "sustained advocacy by AMSA, alongside partners including Movember and Healthy Male." Black Dog and the Danny Frawley Centre — both named in file 01's mental-fitness register — are downstream of a Movember-led ask.

Practical read: for the foreseeable future, the Commonwealth men's-health funding channel runs through, or alongside, Movember. Competing with Movember for that channel is not realistic for a pre-pilot charity. Being a fundable delivery partner inside it is. Note that MAOTG is delivered by 26 grassroots partners — Movember's stated model is explicitly to fund and equip local deliverers.

What they measure — and what they don't

Measured and published: dollars raised · registered participants · program expenditure by cause area · reach counts (MAOTG 64,000+ since 2021 across six countries, 22,000+ in FY25 alone public organisational claim) · practitioner confidence and competence (Men in Mind) · literacy, help-seeking intention, resilience (MAOTG trial) · cost per participant ($37.47).

Not published / unknown: - Dosage for any programme — no session length, session count, or frequency published for MAOTG, Men in Mind, Family Man, MindMoves or Level Up. verified absence The single largest men's-health funder in the world does not publish how long its flagship program takes. - Retention or repeat participation in any digital product. verified absence - Whether MAOTG's literacy and resilience gains persist. No follow-up beyond the trial window was located. unknown - Suicide-rate outcomes attributable to any Movember program. verified absence - Loneliness/connection outcomes despite the connection thesis. verified absence - MindMoves outcomes — the FY25 report describes benefits ("better recognition… increased confidence… reduced stigma… increased willingness") with no design, n, instrument or comparison group stated. public organisational claim

What MFC can learn

  1. Fund the evidence before you need it, and publish the nulls. The MAOTG trial's null results on stigma, informal help-seeking and implicit beliefs are in the public record. That is what makes the positive findings credible.
  2. Own a policy ask, not just a program. $32m of Commonwealth money existed because one organisation wrote a platform. MFC will never do this at Movember's scale — but the mechanism (define the ask, bring the sector, present to both parties) is scale-independent.
  3. Fund-and-equip beats build-and-deliver for reach. 26 grassroots partners deliver MAOTG. File 11 already established that MFC's facilitator-time scaling curve is bad; this is the sector's answer to that problem.
  4. A protocol travels further than an organisation. Movember adopted R U OK?'s ALEC. Whoever owns the four-step verb owns the category's operating instruction.
  5. Publish cost per participant. $37.47 is a number a funder can act on. Almost nobody else in this report publishes one.

What MFC should NOT imitate

  • The residual-percentage impact pie. 78.9% is arithmetic, not expenditure. MFC should publish actual program spend as a share of revenue and explain any surplus in the same breath.
  • Summarising a trial into an outcome the trial did not report. The "reduces psychological distress" sentence is the exact thing K-08 exists to prevent.
  • An evidence page built on predecessor programs. Family Man's evidence is ParentWorks' and AccessEI's evidence. MFC will be asked for MFC's.
  • Publishing reach without dosage. 64,000 participants with no published session structure is exposure, not training — the same critique file 02 makes of Smiling Mind and Gotcha4Life.
  • Migrating your category language before your content is ready. Five of six locales currently 404 on the URL every one of their mental-health pages redirects to. inference MFC's own language migration should ship content and URL together.

What they do, and dosage — the clearest published dosage ladder in the sector

verified fact A three-tier, industry-embedded, peer-led model:

Tier Duration Who Purpose
General Awareness Training (GAT) 45 minutes, on site, en masse At least 80% of workers on a site Site becomes "inducted"
Connector Training half-day (duration on public pages varies) partially verified Volunteers who opt up after GAT Keep someone safe in a crisis while connecting them to help
ASIST two days A smaller subset Advanced safe-planning skills

This is the most transferable structural idea in this file for MFC. inference MATES does not try to make everyone competent. It makes everyone aware in 45 minutes, then lets a self-selecting minority climb. The site — not the individual — is the unit of intervention, and the 80% threshold is what makes it an environment change rather than a training event. It is a dosage ladder with an explicit population coverage rule. Nothing else profiled in this project has one.

verified fact Over 100,000 GAT completions nationally across four Australian states (figure reported in the 2023 systematic review; current total unknown).

Evidence base — forensic

Doran, C.M., Gullestrup, J., et al. (2023). "Effectiveness of the Australian MATES in Construction Suicide Prevention Program: a systematic review." Health Promotion International, 38(4), daad082. 12 peer-reviewed articles, Jan 2010 – Feb 2023 (9 construction, 2 coal mining, 1 energy). verified fact

What it found: - Five large studies (n = 2,977 to 20,125) showed statistically significant pre-to-post improvements in mental health and suicide literacy, ranging 2.6% to 27.2%. - Public stigma improved 15.7% (friends) and 15.1% (workmates) over 18 months. Structural stigma 16.0%, p = 0.07 — not significant. - Help-offering intentions maintained improvement at 3-month follow-up — the program's core objective. - Connector training: 16.67% improvement in noticing struggling colleagues. - Suicide rates: −3% per year among construction workers vs −1.5% among other employed men (p<0.001). One Queensland study found a 7.9% risk reduction, not significant.

What it explicitly did NOT establish verified fact: - Causality for the suicide-rate difference — the authors state they cannot attribute the reduction definitively to MATES. - Sustained literacy gains — most improvements were lost by 3-month follow-up, except help-offering. - Cultural shift ("MATES as a way of doing business"), work-environment change, or diffusion. - No formal risk-of-bias assessment was conducted. 9 of 12 studies were simple pre-post with no control group. Only one had a comparison group. "No experimental studies... conducted to date." Attrition was severe (n=2,977 → n=245).

Conflicts of interest, declared verified fact: Jorgen Gullestrup was CEO of MATES in Construction Queensland until June 2021. Anthony LaMontagne is an unpaid member of the MATES in Construction Australia Board. The journal's Editor-in-Chief was recused.

Verdict. inference MATES has the best population-level signal in Australian men's suicide prevention and the honest admission that it cannot claim it. The −3% vs −1.5% comparison is the most-cited number in the field; it is an ecological association from a review co-authored by the program's former CEO, with no controlled trial underneath it. MFC may cite it — but must cite it exactly that way, or it becomes the Smiling-Mind-funding error in a new costume.

Construct claimed · "mental fitness" language

Construct: suicide literacy, stigma, and help-offering (not help-seeking — the model's deliberate inversion). verified fact "Mental fitness": not used. Vocabulary is mateship, awareness, connector, help-offering, suicide prevention. verified — as far as public pages reach

Honest strategic read for MFC

  • The 80%-of-site coverage rule is the idea to steal. MFC's equivalent question — what proportion of a team, club or workplace must complete the entry tier for the environment to change? — is currently unasked anywhere in MFC's design.
  • "Help-offering, not help-seeking" is a genuine construct innovation and it is the same insight R U OK? monetised. MFC's framing should be checked against it: is MFC training people to manage themselves, or to notice others? The answer changes the whole product.
  • Do not imitate the evidence posture. Nine pre-post studies without controls, published over 15 years, would not clear a 2026 funder.
  • Do not imitate the revenue structure. 59.3% government, deficits at the top.

Sources: Doran, Gullestrup et al. 2023, Health Promotion International · PMC full text · mates.org.au — how MATES works · ACNC 2024 AIS dataset — accessed 2026-08-06

MC-05 — GOTCHA4LIFE: relationships only (profiled in file 02, not re-profiled)

verified fact Gotcha4Life executes much of its workshop delivery through Tomorrow Man, Tomorrow Woman and Man Anchor — two of the four organisations in MC-03.

inference The workshop-delivery tier is not four independent competitors; it is a supply chain. Gotcha4Life owns the brand and the language ("mental fitness", "emotional muscle", "meaningful mateship") and buys the facilitation. Tomorrow Man and Man Anchor own the facilitation capacity and rent it out. The Man Cave and Menslink are the two that do both themselves.

strategic hypothesis This creates a real strategic option MFC has not considered. MFC does not have to choose between "build a facilitator bench" and "don't deliver." There is an existing, contractable facilitation market in Australian men's mental health, and its two largest suppliers already work for MFC's closest category-language competitor. MFC could buy delivery capacity the same way Gotcha4Life does — which converts MFC's worst scaling problem (facilitator time) into a procurement problem. The counter-risk: renting the same facilitators as Gotcha4Life would make the two products feel identical in the room, at exactly the moment MFC is trying to distinguish its language from theirs.

verified fact Black Dog Institute and the Danny Frawley Centre — both listed in file 01's mental-fitness register — received $2.0m from the Movember-led 2025 federal package for Spud's Game at the Danny Frawley Centre.

inference File 01's mental-fitness claimant register and the Movember funding map are now the same map. Gotcha4Life ← Tomorrow Man / Man Anchor. Movember → AMSA, Healthy Male, Black Dog / Danny Frawley Centre. Australian men's mental health is a small, interlocked, Movember-funded ecosystem, and "mental fitness" is its house language.

Governance — the fact that explains everything else

"Each of our government funders is a Member of the company of Beyond Blue Limited. This means they have prescribed voting rights and join our board meetings." verified fact — Annual Highlights 2024–25, p.30

inference Beyond Blue is not a charity that receives government funding; it is a charity part-owned in governance terms by its government funders. The Commonwealth, all six states and both territories sit inside the company. This is a materially different structure from every other organisation in this report and it is the single most important thing to understand about Beyond Blue's strategic behaviour: it cannot easily take a position its funder-members oppose, and it does not need to compete for renewal in the way an ordinary grantee does.

strategic hypothesis For MFC this cuts both ways. Beyond Blue will not be an agile competitor. It will also never be a neutral referral partner — its board is the government.
